title.en: Volume 50 Biographies 38: Xin Xiong, Yang Ji, Gao Daomu, Qi Jun, Shan Wei, Yuwen Zhongzhi, Fei Mu, Meng Wei
title.raw: 卷五十 列傳第三十八: 辛雄 楊機 高道穆 綦雋 山偉 宇文忠之 費穆 孟威 Volume 50 Biographies 38: Xin Xiong, Yang Ji, Gao Daomu, Qi Jun, Shan Wei, Yuwen Zhongzhi, Fei Mu, Meng Wei

sentences.zh: 辛雄 楊機 高道穆 綦雋 山偉 宇文忠之 費穆 孟威

translations.literal: Xin Xiong, Yang Ji, Gao Daomu, Qi Jun, Shan Wei, Yuwen Zhongzhi, Fei Mu, Meng Wei
translations.idiomatic: Xin Xiong, Yang Ji, Gao Daomu, Qi Jun, Shan Wei, Yuwen Zhongzhi, Fei Mu, and Meng Wei

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十八

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Thirty-Eight
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 38

sentences.zh: 辛雄族祖琛琛子術術族子德源楊機高道穆兄謙之綦俊山偉宇文忠之費穆孟威

translations.literal: Xin Xiong's clansman-ancestor Chen, Chen's son Shu, Shu's clansman-son Deyuan, Yang Ji, Gao Daomu's elder brother Qianzhi, Qi Jun, Shan Wei, Yuwen Zhongzhi, Fei Mu, Meng Wei
translations.idiomatic: Related figures: Xin Xiong's clansman-ancestor Chen; Chen's son Shu; Shu's clansman-son Deyuan; Yang Ji; Gao Daomu's elder brother Qianzhi; Qi Jun; Shan Wei; Yuwen Zhongzhi; Fei Mu; and Meng Wei

sentences.zh: 辛雄，字世賓，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Xin Xiong, courtesy name Shibin, was a native of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Xiong, courtesy name Shibin, was a native of Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父暢，汝南、鄉郡二郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Chang was Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Runan and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang had served as Grand Administrator of both Runan and Xiang commanderies.

sentences.zh: 雄有孝性，居父憂，殆不可識。

translations.literal: Xiong was filial by nature; while in mourning for his father, he was scarcely recognizable.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was deeply filial. During mourning for his father, he was so worn by grief that he was scarcely recognizable.

sentences.zh: 清河王懌為司空，辟為左曹。

translations.literal: When Prince Qinghe Yi was Minister of Works, he recruited Xiong as Left Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qinghe Yi became Minister of Works, he recruited Xiong to serve as Left Assistant.

sentences.zh: 懌遷司徒，仍授左曹。

translations.literal: When Yi was transferred to Minister over the Masses, he still appointed him Left Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was promoted to Minister over the Masses, he kept Xiong in the same post as Left Assistant.

sentences.zh: 雄用心平直，加以閑明政事，經其斷割，莫不悅服。

translations.literal: Xiong's mind was upright and fair, and moreover he was skilled and clear in administrative affairs; cases decided by him all won approval.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was upright and fair-minded, and he handled administrative affairs with clear competence. Every case he decided won general approval.

sentences.zh: 懌每謂人曰：「必也無訟，辛雄有焉。」

translations.literal: Yi often told others, "If there must be no litigation, Xin Xiong has it."
translations.idiomatic: Yi often told others, "If the ideal is that there be no lawsuits at all, Xin Xiong comes closest to it."

sentences.zh: 曆尚書駕部、三公郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as Lang in the Chariot Section of the Secretariat and as Lang of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in the Secretariat's Chariot Section and as a secretary in the office of the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 會沙汰郎官，唯雄與羊深等八人見留，餘悉罷遣。

translations.literal: When court gentlemen were purged, only Xiong and eight others including Yang Shen were retained; all the rest were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: During a purge of court gentlemen, only Xiong and eight others, including Yang Shen, were kept on; all the rest were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 先是，御史中丞、東平王匡復欲輿棺諫諍，尚書令、任城王澄劾匡大不敬，詔恕死。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Censor-in-Chief, Prince of Dongping Kuang, again wished to carry a coffin to remonstrate; the Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, impeached Kuang for great disrespect, and an edict pardoned him from death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Censor-in-Chief, Prince of Dongping Kuang, had again prepared to carry a coffin in remonstrance. The Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, impeached him for gross disrespect, but an edict spared his life.

sentences.zh: 雄奏理匡曰：「竊惟白衣元匡，曆奉三朝，每蒙寵遇，諤諤之性，簡自帝心。

translations.literal: Xiong memorialized in Kuang's defense, saying, "I venture to consider the commoner Yuan Kuang, who has served three reigns and each time received favor; his forthright nature is well known to the imperial heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong submitted a memorial in Kuang's defense: "I consider that Yuan Kuang, though now in common dress, has served three reigns and always enjoyed imperial favor. His outspoken character is well known to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 故高祖錫之以匡名，陛下任之以彈糾。

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Gaozu bestowed on him the name Kuang, and Your Majesty entrusted him with impeachment and correction.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu gave him the name Kuang, meaning 'to set aright,' and Your Majesty has entrusted him with the duty of impeachment and correction.

sentences.zh: 當高肇之時，匡造棺致諫，主聖臣直，卒以無咎。

translations.literal: In Gao Zhao's time, Kuang made a coffin to remonstrate; the ruler was sage and the minister upright, and in the end he went unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: During Gao Zhao's dominance, Kuang made a coffin to remonstrate. The ruler was wise and the minister was upright, and in the end he went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 假欲重造，先帝已容之于前，陛下亦宜寬之於後。」

translations.literal: If he should again make one, the late emperor already indulged him before; Your Majesty should also be lenient afterward."
translations.idiomatic: If he should again prepare a coffin for remonstrance, the late emperor already indulged him once; Your Majesty should show the same forbearance now."

sentences.zh: 未幾，匡除平州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, Kuang was appointed Governor of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Kuang was appointed Governor of Ping Province.

sentences.zh: 右僕射元欽稱雄之美，左僕射蕭寶夤曰：「吾聞遊僕射云：'得如雄者四五人共省事，足矣'今日之賞，何其晚哉！」

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Yuan Qin praised Xiong's excellence; Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin said, "I heard Vice Director You say, 'If one had four or five men like Xiong to handle affairs together, that would be enough.' How late this reward comes!"
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Yuan Qin praised Xiong's excellence. Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin said, "I once heard Vice Director You remark, 'If we had four or five men like Xiong to manage affairs together, that would be enough.' How late this reward has come!"

sentences.zh: 初，廷尉少卿袁翻以犯罪之人，經恩競訴，枉直難明。

translations.literal: At first, Vice Minister of Justice Yuan Fan, because convicted persons, having received grace, all appealed, found guilt and innocence hard to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: At first, Vice Minister of Justice Yuan Fan found that convicted persons, once granted amnesty, all rushed to appeal, making guilt and innocence hard to distinguish.

sentences.zh: 遂奏曾染風聞者，不問曲直，推為獄成，悉不斷理。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized that those once tainted by rumor, without asking right or wrong, should be treated as cases closed and not reviewed at all.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore proposed that anyone once implicated by rumor, regardless of guilt or innocence, should be treated as a closed case and given no further review.

sentences.zh: 詔門下、尚書、廷尉議之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Chancellery, the Secretariat, and the Court of Justice to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Chancellery, the Secretariat, and the Court of Justice to deliberate the matter.

sentences.zh: 雄議曰：「《春秋》之義，不幸而失，寧僭不濫。

translations.literal: Xiong argued, "The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that if one must err, better excessive punishment than excessive leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong argued, "The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that if one must err in judgment, it is better to punish too severely than to pardon too broadly.

sentences.zh: 僭則失罪人，濫乃害善人。

translations.literal: Excessive punishment loses the guilty; excessive leniency harms the good.
translations.idiomatic: Excessive punishment may miss the guilty, but excessive leniency harms the innocent.

sentences.zh: 今議者不忍罪奸吏，使出入縱情，令君子小人，薰蕕不別，豈所謂賞善罰惡，殷勤隱恤者也？

translations.literal: Now the proponents cannot bear to punish corrupt officials, letting them come and go at will, so that gentlemen and petty men, fragrant and foul, are not distinguished—is this what is meant by rewarding good and punishing evil with earnest care?
translations.idiomatic: The proposal would spare corrupt officials and let them act as they please, making no distinction between the upright and the base—is that what is meant by rewarding good and punishing evil with conscientious care?

sentences.zh: 古人唯患察獄之不精，未聞知冤而不理。」

translations.literal: The ancients feared only that trials were not thorough; one never heard of knowing injustice and not redressing it."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients feared only that trials were not thorough enough; they never heard of knowing that injustice existed and refusing to redress it."

sentences.zh: 詔從雄議。

translations.literal: An edict followed Xiong's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict adopted Xiong's view.

sentences.zh: 自後每有疑議，雄與公卿駁難，事多見從。

translations.literal: Afterward, whenever there was a doubtful issue, Xiong debated with the high ministers, and his views were often adopted.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever a doubtful issue arose, Xiong debated with the high ministers, and his views were often adopted.

sentences.zh: 於是公能之名甚盛。

translations.literal: Thus his reputation for public ability became very great.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation for public ability grew accordingly.

sentences.zh: 又為《祿養論》，稱仲尼陳五孝，自天子至於庶人，無致仕之文。

translations.literal: He also wrote a Treatise on Salary and Support, stating that Confucius set forth the Five Filial Duties from Son of Heaven down to commoners, with no text on retirement from office.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a Treatise on Salary and Support, arguing that when Confucius set forth the Five Filial Duties from the Son of Heaven down to commoners, he provided no rule for retirement from office.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》：八十，一子不從政；

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says: at eighty, one son does not attend to government;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says that at eighty, one son may leave government service;

sentences.zh: 九十，家不從政。

translations.literal: at ninety, the household does not attend to government.
translations.idiomatic: and at ninety, an entire household may do so.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注云：「復除之。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: "Exemption from corvée and taxes."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary explains this as "exemption from corvée and taxes."

sentences.zh: 然則止復庶人，非公卿士大夫之謂。

translations.literal: Thus it applies only to commoners, not to grandees, ministers, and scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: That rule applies only to commoners, not to grandees, ministers, and scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 以為宜聽祿養，不約其年。

translations.literal: He held that they should be allowed salary and support without limiting it by age.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that officials should be allowed to receive salary and support without an age limit.

sentences.zh: 書奏，孝明納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Xiaoming accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 後除司空長史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時諸公皆慕其名，欲屈為佐，莫能得也。

translations.literal: At the time all the high lords admired his name and wished to have him as assistant, but none could obtain him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time every leading official admired his reputation and wanted him as an assistant, but none could secure his services.

sentences.zh: 時諸方賊盛，而南寇侵境，山蠻作逆，孝明欲親討，以荊州為先。

translations.literal: At the time bandits were strong in all regions; southern invaders encroached on the borders and mountain barbarians rebelled; Emperor Xiaoming wished to campaign in person, taking Jingzhou first.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were active on every front. Southern invaders pressed the borders, and mountain tribes had risen in rebellion. Emperor Xiaoming planned to campaign in person, beginning with Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 詔雄為行台左丞，與臨淮王彧東趣葉城；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xiong Left Assistant of the Mobile Headquarters, to advance east with Prince of Linhuai Yu toward Yecheng;
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Xiong Left Assistant of the Mobile Headquarters to advance east with Prince of Linhuai Yu toward Yecheng;

sentences.zh: 別將裴衍，西通鴉路。

translations.literal: the separate commander Pei Yan was to open the Ya route in the west.
translations.idiomatic: while the separate commander Pei Yan was to open the Ya route from the west.

sentences.zh: 衍稽留未進，議師已次汝濱。

translations.literal: Yan delayed and did not advance; the deliberative army had already reached the Ru River bank.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan delayed and failed to advance, while the main deliberative army had already reached the Ru River.

sentences.zh: 逢北溝求救，議以處分道別，不欲應之。

translations.literal: They met Beigou seeking rescue; the deliberative council, citing separate routes and positions, did not wish to respond.
translations.idiomatic: When Beigou sent word asking for rescue, the council, citing separate routes and jurisdictions, did not wish to respond.

sentences.zh: 雄曰：「王執麾閫外，唯利是從，見可而進，何必守道？」

translations.literal: Xiong said, "The prince holds command beyond the passes; he should follow advantage, advance when he sees opportunity—why must he keep to the rule?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiong said, "Your Highness holds command beyond the passes. You should follow advantage and advance when opportunity appears—why insist on rigid rules?"

sentences.zh: 彧恐後有得失之責，要雄符下。

translations.literal: Yu, fearing later blame for gain or loss, demanded that Xiong issue a written order.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, fearing later blame for whatever followed, demanded a written order from Xiong.

sentences.zh: 雄以車駕將親伐，蠻夷必懷震動，乘彼離心，無往不破，遂符彧軍，令速赴擊。

translations.literal: Xiong reasoned that the imperial carriage was about to campaign in person, so the barbarians would surely be shaken; exploiting their disunity, they would be unbeatable wherever they went. He therefore issued orders to Yu's army to hurry and strike.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong reasoned that once the emperor marched in person, the tribes would be shaken, and exploiting their disunity the army could break them wherever it struck. He therefore issued orders to Yu's army to advance at once.

sentences.zh: 賊聞，果自走散。

translations.literal: When the bandits heard, they indeed fled and dispersed on their own.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels heard of the advance, they fled and dispersed on their own.

sentences.zh: 在軍上疏曰：「凡人所以臨堅陳而忘身，觸白刃而不憚者，一則求榮名，二則貪重賞，三則畏刑罰，四則避禍難。

translations.literal: While in the army he submitted a memorial saying, "The reason ordinary men face solid formations and forget themselves, meet bare blades and do not fear, is first to seek glory, second to covet rich reward, third to fear punishment, fourth to avoid disaster.
translations.idiomatic: While with the army he submitted a memorial: "Ordinary men face solid battle lines and forget themselves, meet naked blades and do not flinch, for four reasons: to seek glory, to covet rich reward, to fear punishment, and to avoid disaster.

sentences.zh: 非此數事，雖聖王不能勸其臣，慈父不能厲其子。

translations.literal: Apart from these matters, even a sage king cannot urge his ministers, nor a loving father steel his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Without these incentives, even a sage king cannot move his ministers, nor a loving father stir his sons to action.

sentences.zh: 明主深知其情，故賞必行，罰必信，使親疏貴賤，勇怯賢愚，聞鐘鼓之聲，見旍旗之列，莫不奮激，競赴敵場。

translations.literal: A clear-sighted ruler knows this well, therefore rewards are surely granted and punishments surely enforced, so that whether near or far, noble or base, brave or timid, wise or foolish, at the sound of bells and drums and the sight of banners and flags, none fail to rouse themselves and race to the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler understands this, and therefore makes rewards certain and punishments reliable, so that whether near or far, noble or base, brave or timid, wise or foolish, all who hear drums and bells and see banners and flags rouse themselves and race to the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 豈厭久生而樂早死也？

translations.literal: Do they hate long life and delight in early death?
translations.idiomatic: It is not that they hate long life and welcome early death.

sentences.zh: 利害縣於前，欲罷不能耳。

translations.literal: Gain and harm hang before them; they wish to stop but cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Gain and harm hang before them, and they cannot hold back even if they wished to.

sentences.zh: 自秦、隴逆節，將歷數年，蠻左亂常，稍已多載。

translations.literal: Since Qin and Long broke away, it will soon be several years; barbarian disturbances in the south have already lasted many years.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion in Qin and Long had already lasted several years, and disturbances among the southern tribes had gone on even longer.

sentences.zh: 凡在戎役，數十萬人，三方之師，敗多勝少，跡其所由，不明賞罰故也。

translations.literal: All told in military service were several hundred thousand men; armies on three fronts won less and lost more—the trace of the cause is unclear rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred thousand men were under arms on three fronts, yet our armies lost more often than they won. The reason is that rewards and punishments have not been clear.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲天下之早平，湣征夫之勤悴，乃降明詔，賞不移時。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes the realm pacified early and pities the toil of the campaigners, and therefore issued a clear edict that rewards should not be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty wishes to pacify the realm quickly and pities the toil of the soldiers, and has issued a clear edict that rewards must not be delayed.

sentences.zh: 然兵將之勳，曆稔不決，亡軍之卒，晏然在家，致令節士無所勸慕，庸人無所畏懾。

translations.literal: Yet the merit of officers and generals goes undecided for years, and soldiers who lost their armies sit calmly at home, so that men of integrity have nothing to emulate and common men have nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the merits of officers and generals go undecided for years, while soldiers who abandoned their units sit calmly at home. Men of integrity have nothing to emulate, and common soldiers have nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 進而擊賊，死交而賞賒；

translations.literal: Advance and strike the bandits—death is immediate but reward is deferred;
translations.idiomatic: Advance against the enemy and death is immediate, but reward is deferred;

sentences.zh: 退而逃散，身全而無罪，此其所以望敵奔沮，不肯進力者矣。

translations.literal: retreat and flee—body intact and no guilt: this is why they gaze at the enemy and break in spirit, unwilling to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: retreat and flee and one keeps body and life without penalty. That is why men lose heart at the sight of the enemy and refuse to fight with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 為重發明詔，更量賞罰，則軍威必張，賊難可弭。

translations.literal: If a clear edict is reissued and rewards and punishments are reassessed, then military prestige will surely expand and bandit troubles can be quelled.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty reissues a clear edict and reassesses rewards and punishments, military prestige will rise and the rebels can be subdued.

sentences.zh: 臣聞必不得已，去食就信，以此推之，信不可斯須廢也。

translations.literal: I have heard that when there is no choice, one gives up food and keeps faith; by this reasoning, faith cannot be abandoned even for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when there is no choice, one may give up food but not faith. By that measure, trust cannot be set aside even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 賞罰，陛下之所易，尚不能全而行之；

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments are what Your Majesty can easily control, yet they still cannot be fully carried out;
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments lie entirely within Your Majesty's power, yet even these cannot be fully enforced;

sentences.zh: 攻敵，士之所難，欲其必死，寧可得也？」

translations.literal: attacking the enemy is what soldiers find hard—can one expect them to die without fail?"
translations.idiomatic: and attacking the enemy is what soldiers find hardest—how then can we expect them to fight to the death?"

sentences.zh: 後為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Later he became Lang of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Lang in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮入洛，河陰之難，人情未安，雄潛竄不出。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and the disaster at Heyin occurred, popular sentiment was unsettled; Xiong hid and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and the massacre at Heyin followed, public sentiment was unsettled, and Xiong went into hiding.

sentences.zh: 孝莊欲以雄為尚書，門下奏曰：「辛雄不出，存亡未知。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang wished to appoint Xiong Minister; the Chancellery memorialized, "Xin Xiong has not come forth; whether he lives or dies is unknown."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang wished to appoint Xiong Minister, but the Chancellery memorialized, "Xin Xiong has not come forth, and no one knows whether he is alive or dead."

sentences.zh: 孝莊曰：「寧失亡而用之，可失存而不用也？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang said, "Better to use him though lost than not use him though alive—can one?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang said, "Would I rather appoint a man who may be dead than fail to use one who is alive?"

sentences.zh: 遂除度支尚書。

translations.literal: He was therefore appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was therefore appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 後以本官兼侍中、關西尉勞大使。

translations.literal: Later, retaining his original office, he was also made Palace Attendant and Grand Envoy to Console the Troops in Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He later retained his post while also serving as Palace Attendant and Grand Envoy to console the troops in Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 將發，請事五條：一言逋懸租調，宜悉不征；

translations.literal: Before setting out he requested five measures: first, that overdue and suspended land tax and cloth levy should all go uncollected;
translations.idiomatic: Before setting out he proposed five measures: first, that all overdue and suspended land tax and cloth levies should be waived;

sentences.zh: 二言簡罷非時徭役，以紓人命；

translations.literal: second, that irregular corvée at improper times should be reduced and abolished to ease men's lives;
translations.idiomatic: second, that irregular corvée levied at improper times should be reduced or abolished to ease the people's burden;

sentences.zh: 三言課調之際，使豐儉有殊，令州郡量檢，不得均一；

translations.literal: third, that when assessing levies, abundance and scarcity should differ, letting provinces and commanderies measure and inspect without uniform rates;
translations.idiomatic: third, that when assessing levies, rich and poor districts should be treated differently, with provinces and commanderies making local assessments rather than applying a single rate;

sentences.zh: 四言兵起歷年，死亡者眾，或父或子，辛酸未歇，見存耆老，請假板職，悅生者之意，慰死者之魂；

translations.literal: fourth, that war had lasted years and the dead were many, whether fathers or sons; grief had not ceased—let surviving elders be granted provisional appointments to please the living and comfort the spirits of the dead;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, that after years of war with countless dead, whether fathers or sons, surviving elders should be granted provisional appointments to honor the living and comfort the dead;

sentences.zh: 五言喪亂既久，禮儀罕習，如有閨門和穆，孝悌卓然者，宜旌其門閭。

translations.literal: fifth, that disorder had lasted long and ritual was seldom practiced—if any household was harmonious within and outstanding in filial piety and brotherly duty, their gate and lane should be honored.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, that after long disorder, when ritual was seldom practiced, households noted for harmony, filial piety, and brotherly duty should be publicly honored.

sentences.zh: 莊帝從之，因詔：人年七十者授縣，八十授郡，九十加四品將軍，百歲從三品將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang accepted, and therefore issued an edict: at seventy one received a county appointment, at eighty a commandery appointment, at ninety the added title of Fourth-Rank General, at one hundred the Concurrent Third-Rank General.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang accepted, and issued an edict granting county rank to those aged seventy, commandery rank at eighty, the added title of Fourth-Rank General at ninety, and Concurrent Third-Rank General at one hundred.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, he was concurrently Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he was additionally appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時近習專恣，雄懼其讒匿，不能守正，論者頗譏之。

translations.literal: At the time close favorites acted with arbitrary power; Xiong feared their slander and concealment and could not uphold rectitude—commentators somewhat ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: Close favorites held arbitrary power at court, and Xiong, fearing their slander, failed to uphold rectitude—a point on which critics found fault with him.

sentences.zh: 孝武南狩，雄兼左僕射，留守京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu went south on campaign, Xiong was concurrently Left Vice Director and remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched south, Xiong served concurrently as Left Vice Director and remained to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 永熙末，兼侍中。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongxi, he was concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongxi he was additionally appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝入關右，齊神武至洛，於永寧寺大集朝士，責雄及尚書崔孝芬、劉廞、楊機等曰：「為臣奉主，匡危救亂。

translations.literal: The emperor entered Guanxi; Gao Huan of Qi reached Luoyang and at Yongning Temple gathered the court grandees in great assembly, rebuking Xiong and Ministers Cui Xiaofen, Liu Yin, Yang Ji, and others, saying, "As ministers serving a ruler, one should set aright danger and rescue disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled into Guanxi, Gao Huan of Qi reached Luoyang and summoned the court at Yongning Temple. He rebuked Xiong and Ministers Cui Xiaofen, Liu Yin, Yang Ji, and others: "As ministers serving a ruler, your duty is to set aright danger and rescue the realm from disorder.

sentences.zh: 若處不諫諍，出不陪隨，緩則耽寵，急便竄避，臣節安在？」

translations.literal: If at court you do not remonstrate, and when out you do not accompany—when things are calm you indulge in favor, when urgent you flee and hide—where is the integrity of a minister?"
translations.idiomatic: If you do not remonstrate at court, do not accompany the ruler in flight, indulge in favor when times are calm, and flee when danger comes—where is your integrity as ministers?"

sentences.zh: 乃誅之。

translations.literal: He then executed them.
translations.idiomatic: He then had them executed.

sentences.zh: 二子，士璨、士貞，逃入關中。

translations.literal: His two sons, Shican and Shizhen, fled into Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons, Shican and Shizhen, fled into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 雄從父兄纂，字伯將，學涉文史，溫良雅正。

translations.literal: Xiong's elder paternal cousin Zuan, courtesy name Bojiang, had learning that covered literature and history and was gentle, good, refined, and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's elder paternal cousin Zuan, courtesy name Bojiang, was learned in literature and history and was gentle, refined, and upright.

sentences.zh: 初為袞州安東府主簿，與秘書丞同郡李伯尚有舊。

translations.literal: At first he served as Registrar in the Andong Office of Gunzhou and had an old connection with Li Boshang, Secretariat Gentleman, who was from the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Registrar in the Andong Office of Gunzhou and had an old friendship with Li Boshang, a Secretariat Gentleman from his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 伯尚與咸陽王禧同逆，逃竄投纂，事覺，坐免官。

translations.literal: Boshang joined Xianyang Prince Xi in rebellion, fled and went to Zuan; when the matter was discovered, Zuan was implicated and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Boshang joined Xianyang Prince Xi in rebellion, he fled to Zuan. The affair was discovered, and Zuan was implicated and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 後為太尉騎兵參軍，每為府主清河王懌所賞。

translations.literal: Later he became Cavalry Administrative Aide to the Grand Commandant and was repeatedly appreciated by the office head, Prince Yi of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Cavalry Administrative Aide to the Grand Commandant and was repeatedly praised by his office head, Prince Yi of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 至定考，懌曰：「辛騎兵有學有才，宜為上第。」

translations.literal: When the fixed evaluation came, Yi said, "Cavalryman Xin has learning and talent and should be in the highest grade."
translations.idiomatic: When performance ratings were fixed, Yi said, "Cavalryman Xin has both learning and talent and should receive the highest grade."

sentences.zh: 及梁將曹義宗攻新野，詔纂為荊州軍司。

translations.literal: When the Liang general Cao Yizong attacked Xinye, an edict made Zuan Military Administrator of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang general Cao Yizong attacked Xinye, Zuan was appointed by edict as Military Administrator of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 纂善撫將士，人多用命，賊甚憚之。

translations.literal: Zuan was good at soothing generals and soldiers; many men obeyed orders, and the rebels greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan was skilled at caring for officers and soldiers, so the men obeyed orders and the enemy greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 會孝明崩諱至，咸以對敵，欲秘凶問。

translations.literal: It happened that the tabooed news of Emperor Xiaoming's death arrived; all, because they faced the enemy, wished to keep the dire report secret.
translations.idiomatic: Just then news arrived of Emperor Xiaoming's death. Since they were facing the enemy, everyone wanted to keep the dire report secret.

sentences.zh: 纂曰：「安危在人，豈關是也？」

translations.literal: Zuan said, "Safety and danger lie in men; how could they depend on this?"
translations.idiomatic: Zuan said, "Safety and danger depend on men; how could they hinge on this?"

sentences.zh: 遂發喪號哭，三軍縞素，還入州城，申以盟約。

translations.literal: He then announced the mourning and wailed; the three armies wore plain white, returned into the provincial city, and renewed the covenant with them.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore announced the mourning and wailed aloud. The whole army put on white mourning dress, returned inside the provincial city, and renewed their sworn covenant.

sentences.zh: 尋為義宗所圍，相率固守。

translations.literal: Soon they were surrounded by Yizong and led one another in firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yizong surrounded them, and they held firm together.

sentences.zh: 孝莊即位，除兼尚書，仍行台。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Zuan was appointed concurrent shangshu and continued in the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Zuan was appointed concurrent shangshu and continued to serve in the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後大都督費穆擊義宗禽之，入城，因舉酒屬纂曰：「微辛行台之在斯，吾亦無由建此功也。」

translations.literal: Later Grand Commander Fei Mu attacked Yizong and captured him, entered the city, and then raised wine to Zuan and said, "Had Acting Headquarters Xin not been here, I too would have had no way to establish this achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Later Grand Commander Fei Mu attacked and captured Yizong. After entering the city, he raised a cup to Zuan and said, "Without Acting Headquarters Xin here, I would have had no way to accomplish this feat."

sentences.zh: 永安二年，元顥乘勝至城下，為顥禽之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an, Yuan Hao, riding victory, reached below the walls and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yong'an, Yuan Hao, pressing his victory, reached the city walls and captured him.

sentences.zh: 及孝莊還宮，纂謝不守之罪。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Zuan apologized for the failure to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Zuan apologized for failing to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「于時朕亦北巡，東軍不守，豈卿之過。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "At that time I too went north on tour; the eastern army did not hold—how could it be your fault?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "At that time I too had marched north. The eastern army failed to hold—how could that be your fault?"

sentences.zh: 轉滎陽太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Administrator of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Administrator of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 百姓姜洛生、康乞得者，舊是前太守鄭仲明左右，豪猾偷竊，境內患之。

translations.literal: The commoners Jiang Luosheng and Kang Qide had formerly been attendants of the previous Grand Administrator Zheng Zhongming; they were violent and cunning thieves, a plague within the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Two local men, Jiang Luosheng and Kang Qide, had formerly been retainers of the previous Grand Administrator Zheng Zhongming. Violent and cunning thieves, they were a plague throughout the commandery.

sentences.zh: 纂伺捕禽獲，梟於郡市，百姓欣然。

translations.literal: Zuan watched, captured, and seized them, displayed their heads in the commandery market, and the people were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan tracked them down, captured them, and displayed their heads in the commandery market, to the great satisfaction of the people.

sentences.zh: 纂僑屬洛陽，太昌中，乃為河南邑中正。

translations.literal: Zuan was a sojourner affiliated with Luoyang; in Taichang he became Rectifier of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan was registered as a sojourner in Luoyang, and in the Taichang era he became Rectifier of Henan.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年，除河內太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, he was appointed Grand Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he was appointed Grand Administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 齊神武赴洛，兵集城下，纂出城謁，神武慰勉之。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan of Qi came to Luoyang and troops gathered below the walls, Zuan went out to pay respects; Gao Huan consoled and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan marched on Luoyang and his troops gathered below the walls, Zuan went out to pay his respects, and Gao Huan consoled and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 因命前侍中司馬子如曰：「吾行途疲弊，宜代吾執河內手也。」

translations.literal: He then ordered former Palace Attendant Sima Ziru, saying, "I am weary from the march; you should take my place and hold Henei for me."
translations.idiomatic: He then told former Palace Attendant Sima Ziru, "I am worn out from the march. You should take my place and hold Henei for me."

sentences.zh: 尋為兼尚書、南道行台、西荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Minister, Mobile Headquarters of the Southern Route, and Governor of Xijingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed concurrently Minister, commander of the Southern Route Mobile Headquarters, and Governor of West Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 時蠻酋樊大能應西魏，纂攻之，不克而敗，為西魏將獨孤信所害。

translations.literal: At the time the barbarian chieftain Fan Daneng responded to Western Wei; Zuan attacked him, failed to overcome him and was defeated, and was killed by the Western Wei general Dugu Xin.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribal chieftain Fan Daneng sided with Western Wei, Zuan attacked him, failed, and was killed by the Western Wei general Dugu Xin.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Duke of the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Duke of the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 雄族祖琛。

translations.literal: Xiong's clansman-ancestor Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's clansman-ancestor Chen.

sentences.zh: 琛字僧貴。

translations.literal: Chen's courtesy name was Senggui.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's courtesy name was Senggui.

sentences.zh: 祖敬宗，父樹寶，並代郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jingzong and father Shubao were both Grand Administrators of Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jingzong and his father Shubao had both served as Grand Administrator of Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 琛少孤，曾過友人，見其父母無恙，垂涕久之。

translations.literal: Chen was orphaned young; once passing a friend's home and seeing his parents unharmed, he wept for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was orphaned young. Once, visiting a friend and seeing his parents alive and well, he wept for a long time.

sentences.zh: 釋褐奉朝請、滎陽郡丞。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the hemp he served as Court Gentleman for Attendance and Assistant Grand Administrator of Xingyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering office he served as Court Gentleman for Attendance and Assistant Grand Administrator of Xingyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 太守元麗性頗使酒，琛每諫之。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Yuan Li was rather given to wine; Chen often remonstrated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator Yuan Li was rather given to drink, and Chen often remonstrated with him.

sentences.zh: 麗後醉，輒令閉閣，曰：「勿使丞入也。」

translations.literal: Later when Li was drunk, he would have the gate closed and say, "Do not let the Assistant in."
translations.idiomatic: When Li was drunk afterward, he would have the gate closed and say, "Do not let the Assistant in."

sentences.zh: 孝文南征，麗從輿駕，詔琛曰：「委卿郡事，如太守也。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south, Li followed the imperial carriage; an edict told Chen, "I entrust the commandery affairs to you, as to the Grand Administrator."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen campaigned south, Li accompanied the imperial carriage. An edict told Chen, "I entrust the commandery to you as though you were Grand Administrator."

sentences.zh: 景明中，為揚州征南府長史。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he became Chief Clerk of Yangzhou's Southern Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingming era he became Chief Clerk of the Southern Campaign Headquarters at Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 刺史李崇，多事產業，琛每諫折，崇不從，遂相糾舉，詔並不問。

translations.literal: Inspector Li Chong was much occupied with property ventures; Chen often remonstrated and rebuked him, but Chong would not listen, so they impeached each other; an edict ordered that neither be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Li Chong was much occupied with business ventures. Chen often remonstrated with him, but Chong would not listen, so they impeached each other. An edict ordered that neither be questioned.

sentences.zh: 後加龍驤將軍、南梁太守。

translations.literal: Later he was additionally made General of Dragon Cavalry and Grand Administrator of Nanliang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later additionally appointed General of Dragon Cavalry and Grand Administrator of Nanliang.

sentences.zh: 崇因置酒謂琛曰：「長史後必為刺史，但不知得上佐何如人耳。」

translations.literal: Chong therefore set out wine and told Chen, "The Chief Clerk will surely become an Inspector later, but one does not know what sort of chief assistant he will get."
translations.idiomatic: Chong set out wine and told Chen, "You will surely become an inspector one day, though one cannot know what sort of chief assistant you will have."

sentences.zh: 琛對曰：「若萬一叨忝，得一方正長史，朝夕聞過，是所願也。」

translations.literal: Chen replied, "If by some chance I should undeservedly receive the post, to have an upright Chief Clerk and hear of my faults morning and evening—that is what I would wish."
translations.idiomatic: Chen replied, "If by some chance I should receive such a post, I would wish for an upright chief clerk who would tell me of my faults morning and evening."

sentences.zh: 崇有慚色。

translations.literal: Chong showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Chong looked ashamed.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 琛寬雅有度量，涉獵經史，喜慍不形於色。

translations.literal: Chen was generous and refined, with breadth of mind; he ranged through the classics and histories, and joy and anger did not show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was generous and refined, with breadth of mind. He ranged widely through the classics and histories, and neither joy nor anger showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 當官奉法，所在有稱。

translations.literal: In office he upheld the law, and wherever he served he won praise.
translations.idiomatic: In office he upheld the law, and wherever he served he won praise.

sentences.zh: 長子悠，字元壽，早有器業，為侍御史，監揚州軍。

translations.literal: His eldest son You, courtesy name Yuanshou, showed early talent and capacity; he was Attending Censor and supervised the Yangzhou army.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son You, courtesy name Yuanshou, showed early talent and capacity. He served as Attending Censor supervising the Yang Province army.

sentences.zh: 賊平，錄勳書，時李崇猶為刺史，欲寄人名，悠不許。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, merit records were compiled; Li Chong was still Inspector and wished to insert other men's names, but You would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified and merit records were compiled, Li Chong, still serving as inspector, wished to insert other men's names, but You would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「我昔逢其父，今復逢其子。」

translations.literal: Chong said, "I once met his father; now I meet his son again."
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "I once crossed paths with his father; now I cross paths with his son again."

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: You died young.

sentences.zh: 悠弟俊，字叔義，有文才。

translations.literal: You's younger brother Jun, courtesy name Shuyi, had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: You's younger brother Jun, courtesy name Shuyi, had literary talent.

sentences.zh: 魏子建為山南行台，以為郎中。

translations.literal: When Wei Zijian was Mobile Headquarters of the Southern Mountains, he appointed Jun Lang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zijian commanded the Southern Mountains Mobile Headquarters, he appointed Jun as a secretary.

sentences.zh: 有軍國機斷。

translations.literal: He had decisive judgment in military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had decisive judgment in military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 還京，于滎陽為人所劫害。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, at Xingyang he was robbed and killed by men.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to the capital he was robbed and killed at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 贈東秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Governor of Dongqinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Governor of East Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 俊弟術。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's younger brother Shu.

sentences.zh: 術字懷哲，少明敏，有識度，解褐司空胄曹參軍。

translations.literal: Shu, courtesy name Huaizhe, was bright and keen from youth, with insight and judgment; upon leaving the hemp he became Army Aide in the Minister of Works' Heir Apparent Office.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, courtesy name Huaizhe, was bright and keen from youth and showed insight and judgment. Upon entering office he became an aide in the Heir Apparent Office of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 與僕射高隆之共典營構鄴都宮室。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Director Gao Longzhi he oversaw the construction of the palace buildings at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Vice Director Gao Longzhi he oversaw construction of the palace buildings at Ye.

sentences.zh: 術有思理，百工克濟。

translations.literal: Shu had thoughtful planning, and all the crafts were successfully completed.
translations.idiomatic: Shu planned thoughtfully, and all the crafts were successfully completed.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書右丞，出為清河太守，政有能名。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat, then sent out as Grand Administrator of Qinghe, where his administration won a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat, then sent out as Grand Administrator of Qinghe, where his administration won a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 追授并州長史，遭父憂去職。

translations.literal: He was retroactively appointed Chief Clerk of Bingzhou, but left office upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was retroactively appointed Chief Clerk of Bing Province but left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 清河父老數百人，詣闕上書，請立碑頌德。

translations.literal: Several hundred elders of Qinghe went to the palace gates and submitted a memorial requesting a stele to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred elders of Qinghe went to the palace and submitted a memorial requesting a stele in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄嗣事，與尚書左丞宋遊道、中書侍郎李繪等並追詣晉陽，俱為上客。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang of Qi succeeded to affairs, together with Left Assistant Director Song Youdao, Secretariat Gentleman Li Hui, and others he was summoned to Jinyang and all became honored guests.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang of Qi succeeded to power, Shu was summoned to Jinyang together with Left Assistant Director Song Youdao, Secretariat Gentleman Li Hui, and others, and all were treated as honored guests.

sentences.zh: 累遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 武定六年，侯景叛，除東南道行台尚書，封江夏縣男。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wuding, Hou Jing rebelled; Shu was appointed Minister of the Southeastern Route Mobile Headquarters and enfeoffed as Baron of Jiangxia County.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wuding, when Hou Jing rebelled, Shu was appointed Minister of the Southeastern Route Mobile Headquarters and enfeoffed as Baron of Jiangxia County.

sentences.zh: 與高岳等破侯景，禽蕭明。

translations.literal: Together with Gao Yue and others he defeated Hou Jing and captured Xiao Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Gao Yue and others he defeated Hou Jing and captured Xiao Ming.

sentences.zh: 遷東徐州刺史，為淮南經略使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Dongxuzhou and made Commissioner for Strategy in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of East Xu Province and made Commissioner for Strategy in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 齊天保元年，侯景徵江西租稅，術率諸軍度淮斷之，燒其稻數百萬石。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao of Qi, Hou Jing was collecting land tax west of the river; Shu led the armies across the Huai to cut him off and burned several million shi of his rice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao, when Hou Jing was collecting taxes west of the river, Shu led the armies across the Huai to cut him off and burned several million shi of his rice.

sentences.zh: 還鎮下邳，人隨術北度淮者三千餘家。

translations.literal: Returning to garrison at Xiapi, more than three thousand households followed Shu north across the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to garrison at Xiapi, more than three thousand households followed Shu north across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 東徐州刺史郭志殺郡守，文宣聞之，敕術自今所統十餘州地，諸有犯法者，刺史先啟聽報；

translations.literal: Governor of Dongxuzhou Guo Zhi killed a commandery administrator; when Wensuan heard, he ordered Shu that from now on in the more than ten provinces under his command, for all who violated the law, the Inspector should first memorialize and await approval;
translations.idiomatic: When Governor of East Xu Province Guo Zhi killed a commandery administrator, Wensuan ordered that within the more than ten provinces under Shu's command, inspectors who found lawbreakers must first memorialize and await approval;

sentences.zh: 以下先斷，後表聞。

translations.literal: those below should decide first and report afterward.
translations.idiomatic: officials below that rank might decide first and report afterward.

sentences.zh: 齊代行台兼總人事，自術始也。

translations.literal: In the Qi dynasty, a Mobile Headquarters concurrently overseeing personnel affairs began with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi it was Shu who first held a Mobile Headquarters post with concurrent authority over personnel.

sentences.zh: 安州刺史、臨清太守、盱眙蘄城二鎮將犯法，術皆案奏殺之。

translations.literal: The Governor of Anzhou, Grand Administrator of Linqing, and the two garrison commanders of Xuyi and Qicheng all violated the law; Shu investigated, memorialized, and had them all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Governor of An Province, the Grand Administrator of Linqing, and the garrison commanders of Xuyi and Qicheng all broke the law. Shu investigated each case, memorialized, and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 睢州刺史及所部郡守，俱犯大辟，朝廷以其奴婢百口及貲財盡賜術。

translations.literal: The Governor of Suizhou and the commandery administrators under him all committed capital offenses; the court granted Shu all their hundred-odd slaves and servants and their entire property.
translations.idiomatic: The Governor of Sui Province and the commandery administrators under him all committed capital offenses. The court granted Shu all their slaves and servants—more than a hundred in all—and their entire property.

sentences.zh: 三辭不見許，術乃送詣所司，不復以聞。

translations.literal: He declined three times without being permitted; Shu then sent them to the responsible office and did not report further.
translations.idiomatic: He declined three times without success, then sent everything to the responsible office and made no further report.

sentences.zh: 邢邵聞之，遺術書曰：「昔鐘離意云：孔子忍渴於盜泉，便以珠璣委地。

translations.literal: When Xing Shao heard, he sent Shu a letter saying, "Long ago Zhongli Yi said: Confucius endured thirst at Thief Spring and would cast pearls and jade to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing Shao heard of this, he wrote to Shu: "Long ago Zhongli Yi said that Confucius would endure thirst at Thief Spring rather than drink there, and would cast pearls and jade to the ground rather than keep them.

sentences.zh: 足下今能如此，可謂異代一時。」

translations.literal: That you can do the same today may be called one man across different ages."
translations.idiomatic: That you can do the same today makes you a man of a different age."

sentences.zh: 及王僧辨破侯景，術招攜安撫，城鎮相繼款附，前後二十餘州。

translations.literal: When Wang Sengbian defeated Hou Jing, Shu recruited, gathered, and pacified; walled towns and garrisons submitted in succession, more than twenty provinces in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian defeated Hou Jing, Shu recruited and pacified the region. Walled towns and garrisons submitted in succession—more than twenty provinces in all.

sentences.zh: 於是移鎮廣陵，獲傳國璽送鄴，文宣以璽告於太廟。

translations.literal: He then moved his garrison to Guangling, obtained the Imperial Seal and sent it to Ye; Wensuan announced the seal in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his headquarters to Guangling, obtained the Imperial Seal, and sent it to Ye, where Wensuan announced it in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 此璽即秦所制，方四寸，上紐交盤龍，其文曰：「受命于天，既壽永昌。」

translations.literal: This seal was made by Qin, four inches square, with an interlaced coiled dragon on the knob; its inscription read: "Having received the mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal prosperity."
translations.idiomatic: This seal had been made in Qin. It was four inches square, with an interlaced coiled dragon on the knob, and bore the inscription: "Having received the mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal prosperity."

sentences.zh: 二漢相傳，又曆魏、晉；

translations.literal: It was handed down through the two Han dynasties and passed through Wei and Jin;
translations.idiomatic: It passed through the two Han dynasties and through Wei and Jin;

sentences.zh: 晉懷帝敗，沒于劉聰；

translations.literal: when Emperor Huai of Jin was defeated, it was lost to Liu Cong;
translations.idiomatic: when Emperor Huai of Jin was defeated, it fell into the hands of Liu Cong;

sentences.zh: 聰敗，沒于石氏；

translations.literal: when Cong was defeated, it was lost to the Shi clan;
translations.idiomatic: when Cong was defeated, it passed to the Shi clan;

sentences.zh: 石氏敗，晉穆帝永和中，濮陽太守戴僧施得之，遣督護何融送於建業；

translations.literal: when the Shi clan was defeated, in the Yonghe era of Emperor Mu of Jin, Grand Administrator of Puyang Dai Shishi obtained it and sent Supervisor He Rong to deliver it to Jianye;
translations.idiomatic: when the Shi clan fell, in the Yonghe era of Emperor Mu of Jin, Grand Administrator of Puyang Dai Shishi obtained it and sent Supervisor He Rong to deliver it to Jianye;

sentences.zh: 曆宋、齊、梁；

translations.literal: it passed through Song, Qi, and Liang;
translations.idiomatic: it passed through Song, Qi, and Liang;

sentences.zh: 梁敗，侯景得之；

translations.literal: when Liang was defeated, Hou Jing obtained it;
translations.idiomatic: when Liang fell, Hou Jing obtained it;

sentences.zh: 景敗，侍中趙思賢以璽投景南袞州刺史郭元建，送於術，故術以進焉。

translations.literal: when Jing was defeated, Palace Attendant Zhao Sixian cast the seal to Jing's Governor of Nangunzhou Guo Yuanjian, who sent it to Shu; therefore Shu presented it.
translations.idiomatic: when Jing was defeated, Palace Attendant Zhao Sixian entrusted the seal to Jing's Governor of South Gun Province Guo Yuanjian, who sent it to Shu, and Shu presented it to the court.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為殿中尚書，領太常卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Minister of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as Minister of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Director of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 仍與朝賢，議定律令。

translations.literal: He still joined the court worthies in deliberating on statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the court worthies in deliberating on statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，食南袞州梁郡幹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel, drawing salary from Liang Commandery of Nangunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel, drawing salary from Liang Commandery of South Gun Province.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴以後，大選之職，知名者數四，互有得失，未能盡美。

translations.literal: After the move to Ye, the office of Great Selection had four well-known holders, each with gains and losses, unable to achieve perfection.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Ye, four well-known men held the office of Great Selection in turn. Each had strengths and weaknesses, and none achieved perfection.

sentences.zh: 文襄少年高朗，所弊也疏；

translations.literal: Wenxiang was lofty and bright in youth, but his flaw was laxity;
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang was lofty and bright in youth, but his flaw was laxity;

sentences.zh: 袁叔德沈密謹厚，所傷者細；

translations.literal: Yuan Shude was deep, careful, and sincere, but his harm was excessive minuteness;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shude was deep, careful, and sincere, but his flaw was excessive minuteness;

sentences.zh: 楊愔風流辨給，取士失於浮華；

translations.literal: Yang Yin was elegant and quick in debate, but erred in selecting men by flashiness;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin was elegant and quick in debate, but erred in selecting men for flashiness;

sentences.zh: 唯術性尚貞明，取士以才以器，循名責實，新舊參舉，管庫必擢，門閥不遺。

translations.literal: Only Shu by nature upheld integrity and clarity, selecting men by talent and capacity, matching names to reality; he recommended both new and old, promoting even storehouse clerks and not overlooking noble houses.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shu upheld integrity and clarity. He selected men by talent and capacity, matched names to reality, recommended both newcomers and veterans, promoted even storehouse clerks, and did not overlook men of noble houses.

sentences.zh: 考之前後銓衡，在術最為折衷，甚為當時所稱舉。

translations.literal: Comparing the earlier and later balance-scales of selection, Shu's was the most balanced and was greatly praised by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the earlier and later holders of the office, Shu's selections were the most balanced and won great praise at the time.

sentences.zh: 天保末，文宣嘗令術選百員官，參選者二三千人，術題目士子，人無謗讟，其所旌擢，後亦皆致通顯。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, Wensuan once ordered Shu to select a hundred officials; two or three thousand competed; Shu set topics for the scholars, and no one slandered him; those he honored and promoted later all reached high distinction.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao, Wensuan once ordered Shu to select a hundred officials from two or three thousand candidates. Shu set examination topics for the scholars, and no one slandered him. Those he selected later all reached high distinction.

sentences.zh: 術清儉寡嗜欲，勤於所職，未嘗暫懈，臨軍以威嚴，牧人有惠政。

translations.literal: Shu was pure and frugal with few desires, diligent in his duties and never slack even briefly; commanding armies with stern authority, as a regional governor he had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was pure and frugal, with few desires. He was diligent in his duties and never slack. He commanded armies with stern authority and governed regions with benevolent policies.

sentences.zh: 少愛文史，晚更勤學，雖在戎旅，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: From youth he loved literature and history; in later years he studied even more diligently, and even on campaign he never put down his scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved literature and history. In later years he studied even more diligently, and even on campaign he never put down his books.

sentences.zh: 及定淮南，凡諸貲物，一毫無犯。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified, he did not touch a single item of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan was pacified, he did not touch a single item of plunder.

sentences.zh: 唯大收典籍，多是宋、齊、梁時佳本，鳩集萬餘卷，並顧、陸之徒名畫，二王已下法書，數亦不少。

translations.literal: He only greatly collected classics and books, mostly fine editions from Song, Qi, and Liang, gathering more than ten thousand scrolls, along with famous paintings by Gu, Lu, and others, and calligraphy from the Two Wangs downward—also not a few.
translations.idiomatic: He did, however, collect classics and books on a large scale—mostly fine editions from Song, Qi, and Liang—amassing more than ten thousand scrolls, along with famous paintings by Gu, Lu, and others and calligraphy from the Two Wangs downward, also in considerable number.

sentences.zh: 俱不上王府，唯入私門。

translations.literal: None went to the princely storehouse; all entered his private household.
translations.idiomatic: None of these went to the princely storehouse; all entered his private household.

sentences.zh: 及還朝，頗以饟遺貴要，物議以此少之。

translations.literal: When he returned to court, he often sent gifts to the powerful; public opinion therefore thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court, he often sent gifts to powerful officials, and public opinion thought less of him for it.

sentences.zh: 十年卒，年六十。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 皇建二年，贈開府儀同三司、中書監、青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangjian he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Full Honors, Director of the Secretariat, and Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangjian he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Full Honors, Director of the Secretariat, and Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 子閣卿，尚書郎。

translations.literal: His son Geqing was a Lang of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Geqing served as a secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 閣卿弟衡卿，有識學，開府參軍事。

translations.literal: Geqing's younger brother Hengqing had insight and learning and was Army Aide to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Geqing's younger brother Hengqing had insight and learning and served as army aide to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 隋大業初，卒于太常丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye of Sui he died as Assistant Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daye era of Sui he died while serving as Assistant Director of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 術族子德源。

translations.literal: Shu's clansman-son Deyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's clansman-son Deyuan.

sentences.zh: 德源字孝基，祖穆，魏平原太守。

translations.literal: Deyuan's courtesy name was Xiaoji; his grandfather Mu was Grand Administrator of Pingyuan in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan's courtesy name was Xiaoji. His grandfather Mu had served as Grand Administrator of Pingyuan under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父子馥，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: His father Zifu was Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zifu served as Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 德源沈靜好學，十四解屬文，及長，博覽書記。

translations.literal: Deyuan was calm and quiet, fond of learning; at fourteen he could compose prose, and when grown he read widely in books and records.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan was calm and quiet and fond of learning. At fourteen he could compose prose, and as an adult he read widely in books and records.

sentences.zh: 美儀容，中書侍郎裴讓之特相愛好，兼有龍陽之重。

translations.literal: Handsome in bearing, he was specially loved by Secretariat Gentleman Pei Rangzhi, who also had the weight of Longyang.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in bearing, he was specially favored by Secretariat Gentleman Pei Rangzhi, who also cherished him with the affection of Longyang.

sentences.zh: 齊尚書僕射楊遵彥、殿中尚書辛術皆一時名士，並虛襟禮敬，同舉薦之。

translations.literal: Vice Director of Qi Yang Zunyan and Minister of the Palace Secretariat Xin Shu were both famous men of the age; all opened their hearts in courtesy and jointly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yang Zunyan of Qi and Minister of the Palace Secretariat Xin Shu were both famous men of the age. They treated him with open courtesy and jointly recommended him.

sentences.zh: 後為兼員外散騎侍郎，聘梁使副。

translations.literal: Later he was concurrently Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant and deputy envoy on a mission to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He later served concurrently as Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant and deputy envoy on a mission to Liang.

sentences.zh: 德源本貧素，因使，薄有資裝，遂餉執事，為父求贈，時論鄙之。

translations.literal: Deyuan was originally poor and plain; because of the mission he had a small amount of goods, and therefore sent gifts to those in charge to seek a posthumous grant for his father; opinion of the time despised this.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan had been poor and plain. On the mission he acquired a modest amount of goods and sent gifts to those in charge to seek a posthumous grant for his father—a move that contemporary opinion despised.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎劉逖上表薦德源：弱齡好古，晚節逾厲，枕藉《六經》，漁獵百氏；

translations.literal: Secretariat Gentleman Liu Ti submitted a memorial recommending Deyuan: from youth he loved antiquity, and in later years his zeal grew stronger; he rested on the Six Classics and ranged through the hundred schools;
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Gentleman Liu Ti submitted a memorial recommending Deyuan: from youth he loved antiquity, and in later years his zeal grew stronger. He rested on the Six Classics and ranged through the hundred schools;

sentences.zh: 文章綺豔，體調清華。

translations.literal: his writings were ornate and brilliant, his style clear and refined.
translations.idiomatic: his writings were ornate and brilliant, his style clear and refined.

sentences.zh: 恭慎表於閨門，謙捴著於朋執；

translations.literal: Respect and caution showed within the household, humility and restraint among friends and companions;
translations.idiomatic: Respect and caution showed within his household, humility and restraint among his friends;

sentences.zh: 實後進之辭人，當今之雅器。

translations.literal: truly a literary man among the rising generation, an elegant vessel of the present age.
translations.idiomatic: truly a literary man among the rising generation and an elegant talent of the present age.

sentences.zh: 由是除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Therefore he was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis he was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後兼通直散騎常侍，聘陳。

translations.literal: Later he was concurrently Regular Attendant for Direct Communication and envoy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He later served concurrently as Regular Attendant for Direct Communication and envoy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 及還，待詔文林館，位中書舍人。

translations.literal: When he returned, he awaited edicts at the Wulin Hall and held the post of Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, he awaited edicts at the Wulin Hall and served as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，仕周為宣納上士。

translations.literal: When Qi was destroyed, he served Zhou as Senior Clerk for Proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, he served Zhou as Senior Clerk for Proclamations.

sentences.zh: 因取急詣相州，會尉遲迥起逆，以為中郎，德源辭不獲免，遂亡去。

translations.literal: Because of urgent private business he went to Xiangzhou; he met Yuchi Tong's rebellion and was made Central Commander; Deyuan declined but could not escape appointment, and therefore fled.
translations.idiomatic: On urgent private business he went to Xiang Province, where Yuchi Tong had risen in rebellion. Tong appointed him Central Commander. Deyuan declined but could not escape appointment, and fled.

sentences.zh: 隋受禪，不得調者久之。

translations.literal: When Sui received the abdication, he went long without receiving an appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui received the abdication, he went long without receiving an appointment.

sentences.zh: 隱林慮山，鬱鬱不得志，著《幽居賦》以自寄。

translations.literal: He hid on Mount Linlu, depressed and unfulfilled, and wrote a Rhapsody on Secluded Dwelling to express himself.
translations.idiomatic: He hid on Mount Linlu, depressed and unfulfilled, and wrote a Rhapsody on Secluded Dwelling to express himself.

sentences.zh: 素與武陽太守盧思道友善，時相往來。

translations.literal: He had long been friendly with Grand Administrator of Wuyang Lu Sidao, and at the time they visited each other.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been friendly with Grand Administrator of Wuyang Lu Sidao, and they visited each other at the time.

sentences.zh: 魏州刺史崔彥武奏德源潛為交結，恐有奸計，由是謫令從軍討南寧。

translations.literal: Governor of Weizhou Cui Yanwu memorialized that Deyuan secretly formed connections and might have treacherous designs; therefore he was demoted and ordered to join the army in campaigning against Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Wei Province Cui Yanwu memorialized that Deyuan was secretly forming connections and might have treacherous designs. He was therefore demoted and ordered to join the army campaigning against Nanning.

sentences.zh: 及還，秘書監牛弘以德源才學顯著，奏與著作郎王劭同修國史。

translations.literal: When he returned, Director of the Secretariat Niu Hong, because Deyuan's talent and learning were outstanding, memorialized that he join Compiler Wang Shao in revising the National History.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, Director of the Secretariat Niu Hong, noting Deyuan's outstanding talent and learning, memorialized that he join Compiler Wang Shao in revising the National History.

sentences.zh: 德源每於務隙撰集，注《春秋三傳》三十卷，注《揚子法言》二十三卷。

translations.literal: Deyuan in intervals from his duties compiled and wrote: Commentary on the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, thirty scrolls; Commentary on Yang Xiong's Exemplary Sayings, twenty-three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In intervals from his duties Deyuan compiled a thirty-scroll commentary on the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals and a twenty-three-scroll commentary on Yang Xiong's Exemplary Sayings.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀奏以為掾，轉諮議參軍，卒官。

translations.literal: Prince of Shu Xiu memorialized to appoint him as staff officer; he was transferred to Advisory Army Aide and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shu Xiu memorialized to appoint him as a staff officer. He was transferred to Advisory Army Aide and died in office.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷，又撰《政訓》、《內訓》各二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works of twenty scrolls, and also wrote Political Instruction and Inner Instruction, each twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty scrolls, and also wrote Political Instruction and Inner Instruction, each in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 有子素臣。

translations.literal: He had a son Suchen.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Suchen.

sentences.zh: 德源從祖兄元植，齊天保中，司空司馬。

translations.literal: Deyuan's clansman-elder brother Yuan Zhi, in Tianbao of Qi, was Army Aide to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan's clansman-elder brother Yuan Zhi served as Army Aide to the Minister of Works during the Tianbao era of Qi.

sentences.zh: 學涉，有名聞於世。

translations.literal: Learned and broad in study, he had a reputation known in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and widely read, he enjoyed a reputation in the world.

sentences.zh: 德源族叔珍之，少有氣俠，歷位北海太守，後行平州事，卒於州。

translations.literal: Deyuan's clansman-uncle Zhenzhi, from youth had spirit and chivalry; he successively held the post of Grand Administrator of Beihai, later acted for Pingzhou affairs, and died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan's clansman-uncle Zhenzhi had spirit and chivalry from youth. He served as Grand Administrator of Beihai and later acted as governor of Ping Province, dying in office.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、洛州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Luozhou, with posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Luo Province, with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 子愨，武定末，開府鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: His son Que, at the end of Wuding, was Army Aide in the Armor Section of the Grand Marshal's Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Que, at the end of Wuding, served as Army Aide in the Armor Section of the Grand Marshal's Office.

sentences.zh: 楊機，字顯略，天水冀人也。

translations.literal: Yang Ji, courtesy name Xianlue, was a native of Ji in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji, courtesy name Xianlue, was a native of Ji in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 祖伏恩，徙居洛陽，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fu'en moved to Luoyang and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fu'en moved to Luoyang and established the family there.

sentences.zh: 機少有志節，為士流所稱。

translations.literal: Ji from youth had resolve and integrity and was praised by the scholar class.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ji had resolve and integrity and was praised by the scholar class.

sentences.zh: 河南尹李平、元暉，並召署功曹。

translations.literal: Intendant of Henan Li Ping and Yuan Hui both summoned him to serve as Merit Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Intendants of Henan Li Ping and Yuan Hui both summoned him to serve as Merit Officer.

sentences.zh: 暉尤委以郡事。

translations.literal: Hui especially entrusted him with commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hui especially entrusted him with commandery affairs.

sentences.zh: 或謂暉曰：「弗躬弗親，庶人弗信，何得委事于機，高臥而已。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Hui, "If one does not attend to affairs in person, the common people will not trust him—how can you entrust affairs to Ji and simply lie high?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Hui, "If a ruler does not attend to affairs in person, the people will not trust him. How can you entrust affairs to Ji and simply rest at ease?"

sentences.zh: 暉曰：「吾聞君子勞于求士，逸于任賢，吾既委得其才，何為不可？」

translations.literal: Hui said, "I have heard that the gentleman toils in seeking men of talent and rests in employing the worthy. Since I have entrusted the task to one with ability, why should it not be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "I have heard that a gentleman toils in seeking talent and rests in employing the worthy. Since I have entrusted affairs to a capable man, why should that not suffice?"

sentences.zh: 由是聲名更著。

translations.literal: From this his reputation became even greater.
translations.idiomatic: From this his reputation grew even greater.

sentences.zh: 時皇子國官多非其人，詔選清直之士，機見舉為京兆王愉國中尉，愉甚敬憚之。

translations.literal: At the time many officials of princely states were unfit for their posts; an edict selected pure and upright men; Ji was recommended as Commandant of the State of Prince of Jingzhao Yu, and Yu greatly respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many officials of princely establishments were unfit for their posts. An edict called for pure and upright men, and Ji was recommended as Commandant of Prince of Jingzhao Yu's establishment. Yu greatly respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 後為洛陽令，京輦伏其威風。

translations.literal: Later he became Magistrate of Luoyang; the capital region submitted to his stern authority.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Magistrate of Luoyang, and the capital region submitted to his stern authority.

sentences.zh: 訴訟者一經其前，後皆識其名姓，並記其事理。

translations.literal: Litigants who once passed before him—he afterward knew all their names and remembered the facts of their cases.
translations.idiomatic: Once litigants appeared before him, he afterward remembered their names and the facts of their cases.

sentences.zh: 曆司州別駕、清河內史、河北太守，並有能名。

translations.literal: He successively served as Assistant Inspector of Sizhou, Internal Administrator of Qinghe, and Grand Administrator of Hebei, all with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Assistant Inspector of Si Province, Internal Administrator of Qinghe, and Grand Administrator of Hebei, winning a reputation for ability in each post.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，除度支尚書。

translations.literal: In Yongxi he was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 機方直之心，久而彌厲，奉公正己，為時所稱。

translations.literal: Ji's upright heart grew only sterner with time; upholding fairness and correcting himself, he was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's upright character grew only sterner with time. Upholding fairness and integrity, he was praised by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 家貧無馬，多乘小犢車，時論許其清白。

translations.literal: His household was poor and had no horses; he often rode in a small ox cart, and opinion of the time approved his purity.
translations.idiomatic: His household was poor and had no horses; he often rode in a small ox cart, and contemporary opinion approved his integrity.

sentences.zh: 與辛雄等並為齊神武所誅。

translations.literal: Together with Xin Xiong and others he was executed by Gao Huan of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Xin Xiong and others he was executed by Gao Huan of Qi.

sentences.zh: 高恭之，字道穆，自雲遼東人也。

translations.literal: Gao Gongzhi, courtesy name Daomu, was originally from Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gongzhi, courtesy name Daomu, was originally from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 祖潛，獻文初，賜爵陽關男。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qian, at the beginning of Emperor Xianwen's reign, was granted the title Baron of Yangguan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qian was granted the title Baron of Yangguan at the beginning of Emperor Xianwen's reign.

sentences.zh: 詔以沮渠牧犍女賜潛為妻，封武威公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: An edict granted Qian as wife the daughter of Juqu Mujian, enfeoffed her as Princess of Wuwei, and appointed him Commandant of Escort Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Qian the daughter of Juqu Mujian as his wife, enfeoffed her as Princess of Wuwei, and appointed him Commandant of Escort Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父崇，字積善，少聰敏，以端謹稱。

translations.literal: His father Chong, courtesy name Jishan, was clever and keen from youth and was known for propriety and caution.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chong, courtesy name Jishan, was clever and keen from youth and was known for propriety and caution.

sentences.zh: 家資富厚，而崇志尚儉素。

translations.literal: The household was wealthy, yet Chong's aspiration was frugal simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: The household was wealthy, yet Chong aspired to frugal simplicity.

sentences.zh: 初，崇舅氏坐事誅，公主痛本生絕胤，遂以崇繼牧犍後，改姓沮渠。

translations.literal: At first Chong's maternal uncle was executed for an offense; the princess grieved that her birth line was cut off, and therefore had Chong succeed to Mujian's line and changed his surname to Juqu.
translations.idiomatic: At first Chong's maternal uncle was executed for an offense. The princess grieved that her birth line was cut off and had Chong succeed to Mujian's line, changing his surname to Juqu.

sentences.zh: 景明中，啟復本姓，襲爵，除洛陽令。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he memorialized to restore his original surname, inherited the title, and was appointed Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingming era he memorialized to restore his original surname, inherited the title, and was appointed Magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 為政清斷，吏人畏其威風，發擿不避強禦，縣內肅然。

translations.literal: His administration was clear and decisive; officials and people feared his stern authority; in exposing and impeaching he did not avoid the powerful, and the county was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was clear and decisive. Officials and people feared his stern authority. In exposing wrongdoing he did not avoid the powerful, and the county was orderly.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈滄州刺史，諡曰成。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Governor of Cangzhou, with posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title Governor of Cang Province, with the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 道穆以字行於世，學涉經史，所交皆名流俊士。

translations.literal: Daomu was known in the world by his courtesy name; he ranged through the classics and histories, and those he associated with were all famous and outstanding men.
translations.idiomatic: Daomu was known in the world by his courtesy name. He ranged widely through the classics and histories, and those he associated with were all famous and outstanding men.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事兄如父。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his elder brother as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he served his elder brother as he would a father.

sentences.zh: 每謂人曰：「人生厲心立行，貴於見知，當使夕脫羊裘，朝佩珠玉。

translations.literal: He often told others, "In life one must steel the heart and establish conduct; what is precious is to be recognized—one should shed a sheepskin coat in the evening and wear pearls and jade in the morning.
translations.idiomatic: He often told others, "In life one must steel the heart and establish one's conduct. What matters is to be recognized—one should shed a sheepskin coat in the evening and wear pearls and jade in the morning.

sentences.zh: 若時不我知，便須退跡江海，自求其志。」

translations.literal: If the age does not know me, then one must withdraw to rivers and seas and seek one's own purpose."
translations.idiomatic: If the age does not recognize me, one must withdraw to rivers and seas and seek one's own purpose."

sentences.zh: 御史中尉元匡高選御史，道穆奏記求用於匡，匡遂引為御史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang highly selected censors; Daomu submitted a letter seeking employment under Kuang, and Kuang then recruited him as Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang was selecting censors with great care. Daomu submitted a letter seeking employment under Kuang, and Kuang recruited him as a censor.

sentences.zh: 其所糾擿，不避權豪。

translations.literal: In his impeachments and exposures he did not avoid the powerful and great.
