translations.idiomatic: In his impeachments he did not avoid the powerful and great.

sentences.zh: 正光中，出使相州。

translations.literal: In Zhenguang he went on mission to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguang he went on mission to Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 前刺史李世哲，即尚書令崇之子，多有非法，逼買人宅，廣興屋宇，皆置鴟尾，又于馬埒堠上為木人執節。

translations.literal: The former Inspector Li Shizhe, son of Director of the Secretariat Chong, had many illegal acts: forcing purchase of people's houses, widely building dwellings all with owl-tail roof ornaments, and on the mounds of the horse course setting up wooden men holding insignia.
translations.idiomatic: The former Inspector Li Shizhe, son of Director of the Secretariat Chong, had committed many illegal acts: forcing people to sell their houses, building dwellings on a large scale all with owl-tail roof ornaments, and setting up wooden figures holding insignia on the mounds of the horse course.

sentences.zh: 道穆繩糾，悉毀去之，並表發其贓貨。

translations.literal: Daomu bound and impeached him, had all destroyed, and also memorialized exposing his illicit goods.
translations.idiomatic: Daomu impeached him, had all these destroyed, and memorialized exposing his illicit goods.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮討蠕蠕，道穆監其軍事，榮甚憚之。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong campaigned against the Rouran, Daomu supervised his military affairs; Rong greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong campaigned against the Rouran, Daomu supervised his military affairs, and Rong greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤西征，以為行台郎中，委以軍機之事。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned west, he was made Lang of the Mobile Headquarters and entrusted with military planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned west, Daomu was made secretary of the Mobile Headquarters and entrusted with military planning.

sentences.zh: 後屬兄謙之被害，情不自安，遂托身于孝莊。

translations.literal: Later, because his elder brother Qianzhi was killed, he could not feel secure and therefore placed himself under Xiaozhuang's protection.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his elder brother Qianzhi was killed, he felt insecure and placed himself under Emperor Xiaozhuang's protection.

sentences.zh: 孝莊時為侍中，深相保護。

translations.literal: Xiaozhuang was then Palace Attendant and deeply protected him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhuang was then Palace Attendant and protected him closely.

sentences.zh: 及即位，賜爵龍城侯，除太尉長史，領中書舍人。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he granted Daomu the title Marquis of Longcheng, appointed him Chief Clerk to the Grand Commander, and made him concurrently Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhuang ascended the throne, he granted Daomu the title Marquis of Longcheng, appointed him Chief Clerk to the Grand Commander, and made him concurrently Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 及元顥逼武牢，或勸帝赴關西者，帝以問道穆，道穆言關中殘荒，請車駕北度，循河東下。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed Wulao, some advised the emperor to go to Guanxi; the emperor asked Daomu, and Daomu said Guanzhong was ruined and desolate, and requested that the imperial carriage cross north and follow the river eastward.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao pressed Wulao, some advised the emperor to flee to Guanxi. The emperor asked Daomu, who said Guanzhong was ruined and desolate and urged the imperial carriage to cross north and follow the river eastward.

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 其夜到河內郡北，帝命道穆燭下作詔書，佈告遠近，於是四方知乘輿所在。

translations.literal: That night they reached north of Henei Commandery; the emperor ordered Daomu to draft an edict by candlelight and proclaim it far and near, so that all quarters knew where the imperial carriage was.
translations.idiomatic: That night they reached north of Henei Commandery. The emperor ordered Daomu to draft an edict by candlelight and proclaim it far and near, so that all quarters knew where the imperial carriage was.

sentences.zh: 尋除給事黃門侍郎、安喜縣公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Duke of Anxi County.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Duke of Anxi County.

sentences.zh: 于時爾硃榮欲回師待秋，道穆謂曰：「大王擁百萬之眾，輔天子而令諸侯，此桓、文之舉也。

translations.literal: At the time Erzhu Rong wished to withdraw the army and wait for autumn; Daomu said to him, "Your Highness commands a million men, assists the Son of Heaven and orders the feudal lords—this is an act of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Erzhu Rong wished to withdraw the army and wait for autumn. Daomu said to him, "Your Highness commands a million men, assists the Son of Heaven, and orders the feudal lords—this is an act worthy of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 今若還師，令顥重完守具，可謂養虺成蛇，悔無及矣。」

translations.literal: If you now withdraw, letting Hao again complete his defenses, it may be called raising a small snake until it becomes a great serpent—regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: If you withdraw now and let Hao rebuild his defenses, you will be raising a small snake until it becomes a great serpent—regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 榮深然之。

translations.literal: Rong deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Rong strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 及孝莊反政，因宴次謂爾硃榮曰：「前若不用高黃門計，社稷不安，可為朕勸其酒，令醉。」

translations.literal: When Xiaozhuang resumed power, at a banquet he told Erzhu Rong, "If we had not used Attendant of the Yellow Gate Gao's plan before, the altars of state would not be secure—you may toast him for me and make him drunk."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhuang resumed power, at a banquet he told Erzhu Rong, "If we had not followed Attendant of the Yellow Gate Gao's plan, the altars of state would not be secure. Toast him for me and make him drunk."

sentences.zh: 榮因陳其作監軍時，臨事能決，實可任用。

translations.literal: Rong then stated that when Daomu served as army supervisor, he could decide affairs on the spot and was truly fit for employment.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then stated that when Daomu served as army supervisor he could decide affairs on the spot and was truly fit for employment.

sentences.zh: 尋除御史中尉，仍兼黃門。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and still concurrently held the Yellow Gate post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Censor-in-Chief while still holding his Yellow Gate post.

sentences.zh: 道穆外執直繩，內參機密，凡是益國利人之事，必以奏聞，諫爭盡言，無所顧憚。

translations.literal: Outwardly Daomu held the straight cord of law; inwardly he participated in secrets. Whatever benefited the state and the people he always memorialized; in remonstrance he spoke fully without any hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Daomu upheld the law without favor; inwardly he participated in state secrets. Whatever benefited the state and the people he memorialized, and in remonstrance he spoke fully without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 選用御史，皆當世名輩，李希宗、李繪、陽休之、陽斐、封君義、邢子明、蘇淑、宋世良等三十人。

translations.literal: The censors he selected were all famous men of the age—Li Xizong, Li Hui, Yang Xiuzhi, Yang Fei, Feng Junyi, Xing Ziming, Su Shu, Song Shiliang, and thirty men in all.
translations.idiomatic: The censors he selected were all famous men of the age—Li Xizong, Li Hui, Yang Xiuzhi, Yang Fei, Feng Junyi, Xing Ziming, Su Shu, Song Shiliang, and thirty men in all.

sentences.zh: 于時用錢稍薄，道穆表曰：「百姓之業，錢貨為本，救弊改鑄，王政所先。

translations.literal: At the time the coin in use had grown somewhat thin; Daomu memorialized, saying, "The people's livelihood has money as its foundation; rescuing abuse and recasting coin is what royal government should put first.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the coin in circulation had grown thin. Daomu memorialized: "The people's livelihood rests on money. Rescuing abuse and recasting coin is what royal government should put first.

sentences.zh: 自頃以來，私鑄薄濫，官司糾繩，掛網非一。

translations.literal: Recently private casting of thin and debased coin has been rampant; official prosecutions have caught many in the net.
translations.idiomatic: Recently private casting of thin and debased coin has been rampant, and official prosecutions have caught many offenders.

sentences.zh: 在市銅價，八十一文得銅一斤，私鑄薄錢，斤餘二百。

translations.literal: In the market the price of copper was eighty-one cash for one jin; privately cast thin coin yielded more than two hundred per jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the market copper cost eighty-one cash per jin, while privately cast thin coin yielded more than two hundred per jin.

sentences.zh: 既示之以深利，又隨之以重刑，得罪者雖多，奸鑄者彌眾。

translations.literal: Since great profit was shown them and heavy punishment followed, though many were punished, illicit casters grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Since great profit was shown them and heavy punishment followed, though many were punished, illicit casters grew ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 今錢徒有五銖之文，而無二銖之實，薄甚榆莢，上貫便破，置之水上，殆欲不沈。

translations.literal: Now the coin bears only the inscription of five zhu but has not the substance of two zhu; thin as elm pods, pierced at the top it breaks at once, placed on water it scarcely sinks.
translations.idiomatic: Today's coin bears the inscription of five zhu but has not the substance of two. Thin as elm pods, it breaks when pierced and scarcely sinks when placed on water.

sentences.zh: 因循有漸，科防不切，朝廷失之，彼復何罪。

translations.literal: Through gradual indulgence, penalties and prevention are not strict; if the court loses control, what crime is theirs?
translations.idiomatic: Through gradual indulgence penalties and prevention have grown lax. If the court loses control, what crime is theirs?

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝以五分錢小，改鑄四銖。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han, because the five-fen coin was too small, recast it as four zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han, because the five-fen coin was too small, recast it as four zhu.

sentences.zh: 至武帝復改三銖為半兩。

translations.literal: By Emperor Wu's time it was again changed from three zhu to half a liang.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Wu's time the coin was again changed from three zhu to half a liang.

sentences.zh: 此皆以大易小，以重代輕也。

translations.literal: These all replaced small with large and light with heavy.
translations.idiomatic: In each case small coin was replaced with large and light with heavy.

sentences.zh: 論今據古，宜改鑄大錢，文載年號，以記其始。

translations.literal: Considering the present in light of antiquity, one should recast large coin, its inscription bearing the reign title to mark its beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Considering the present in light of antiquity, one should recast large coin bearing the reign title to mark its beginning.

sentences.zh: 則一斤所成，止七十六文。

translations.literal: Then one jin would yield only seventy-six pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Then one jin would yield only seventy-six pieces.

sentences.zh: 銅價至賤，五十有餘，其中人功，食料、錫炭、鉛鈔，縱復私營，不能自潤。

translations.literal: Copper's price is very low—more than fifty—and among the costs are labor, food, tin, charcoal, and lead alloy; even if cast privately, one cannot profit.
translations.idiomatic: Copper's price is very low—more than fifty cash per jin—and labor, food, tin, charcoal, and lead alloy add further costs. Even private casting would yield no profit.

sentences.zh: 直置無利，自應息心，況復嚴刑廣設也。

translations.literal: With no profit at all, hearts should naturally cease; how much more when severe punishments are broadly set.
translations.idiomatic: With no profit at all, illicit casters should naturally cease—and all the more so when severe punishments are broadly enforced.

sentences.zh: 以臣測之，必當錢貨永通，公私獲允。」

translations.literal: By my estimate, money will surely circulate forever and public and private will both be satisfied."
translations.idiomatic: By my estimate, money will circulate reliably and both public and private interests will be served."

sentences.zh: 後遂用楊侃計，鑄永安五銖錢。

translations.literal: Afterward Yang Kan's plan was adopted and the Yong'an five-zhu coin was cast.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Yang Kan's plan was adopted and the Yong'an five-zhu coin was cast.

sentences.zh: 僕射爾硃世隆當朝權盛，因內見，衣冠失儀，道穆便即彈糾。

translations.literal: Vice Director Erzhu Shilong held great power at court; during an inner audience his dress and cap were out of order, and Daomu immediately impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Erzhu Shilong held great power at court. During an inner audience his dress and cap were out of order, and Daomu immediately impeached him.

sentences.zh: 帝姊壽陽公主行犯清路，執赤棒卒呵之不止，道穆令卒棒破其車。

translations.literal: The emperor's elder sister, Princess of Shouyang, traveled in violation of the cleared road; the soldier with the red staff shouted at her but she would not stop; Daomu ordered the soldier to break her carriage with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's elder sister, Princess of Shouyang, traveled in violation of the cleared road. The soldier with the red staff shouted at her but she would not stop, so Daomu ordered him to break her carriage with the staff.

sentences.zh: 公主深恨，泣以訴帝。

translations.literal: The princess deeply resented this and wept as she complained to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The princess deeply resented this and wept as she complained to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「高中尉清直人，彼所行者公事，豈可私恨責之也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Censor-in-Chief Gao is a pure and upright man; what he did was public business—how can one resent him privately and blame him?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Censor-in-Chief Gao is a pure and upright man. What he did was public business—how can you resent him privately and blame him?"

sentences.zh: 道穆後見帝，帝曰：「一日家姊行路相犯，深以為愧。」

translations.literal: When Daomu later saw the emperor, the emperor said, "The other day my elder sister violated the road rules—I am deeply ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: When Daomu later saw the emperor, the emperor said, "The other day my elder sister violated the road rules, and I am deeply ashamed."

sentences.zh: 道穆免冠謝，帝曰：「朕以愧卿，卿反謝朕！」

translations.literal: Daomu removed his cap and apologized; the emperor said, "I am the one who should feel ashamed before you—yet you apologize to me!"
translations.idiomatic: Daomu removed his cap and apologized. The emperor said, "I am the one who should feel ashamed before you—yet you apologize to me!"

sentences.zh: 尋敕監儀注。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to supervise ritual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to supervise ritual protocol.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「秘書圖籍及典書緗素，多致零落，可令道穆總集帳目，並牒儒學之士，編比次第。」

translations.literal: An edict also said: "Secretariat maps and records and the silk scrolls of the Archive have largely fallen into disorder; Daomu may be ordered to compile the catalog and also dispatch Confucian scholars to arrange them in order."
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered: "Secretariat maps and records and the silk scrolls of the Archive have largely fallen into disorder. Daomu is to compile the catalog and dispatch Confucian scholars to arrange them in order."

sentences.zh: 道穆又上疏曰：「高祖太和之初，置廷尉司直，論刑辟是非，雖事非古始，交濟時要。

translations.literal: Daomu also submitted a memorial, saying, "At the beginning of Taihe under Emperor Gaozu, Direct Rectifiers were placed in the Court of Justice to judge right and wrong in criminal cases; though the office was not ancient in origin, it met the needs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Daomu also submitted a memorial: "At the beginning of Taihe under Emperor Gaozu, Direct Rectifiers were placed in the Court of Justice to judge right and wrong in criminal cases. Though the office was not ancient in origin, it met the needs of the time.

sentences.zh: 竊見御史出使，悉受風聞，雖時獲罪人，亦不無枉濫。

translations.literal: I observe that when censors go on mission they all accept hearsay; though at times they catch the guilty, there is not a little injustice and excess.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that when censors go on mission they accept hearsay. Though they sometimes catch the guilty, there is no little injustice and excess.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 得堯之罰，不能不怨。

translations.literal: Even one who receives Yao's punishment cannot but resent it.
translations.idiomatic: Even one who receives punishment as just as Yao's cannot help resenting it.

sentences.zh: 守令為政，容有愛憎，奸猾之徒，恆思報惡，多有妄造無名，共相誣謗。

translations.literal: Magistrates and prefects in governing may harbor likes and dislikes; crafty and cunning men constantly think of repaying evil, and many falsely create anonymous accusations and slander one another.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates and prefects in governing may harbor likes and dislikes. Crafty men constantly seek revenge, and many falsely create anonymous accusations and slander one another.

sentences.zh: 御史一經檢究，恥於不成，杖木之下，以虛為實。

translations.literal: Once a censor investigates, ashamed of failure, under staff and cudgel he makes the false into fact.
translations.idiomatic: Once a censor investigates, ashamed of failure, he makes the false into fact under staff and cudgel.

sentences.zh: 無罪不能自雪者，豈可勝道哉！

translations.literal: Those innocent who cannot clear themselves—can they be counted?
translations.idiomatic: Those innocent who cannot clear themselves—can they even be counted?

sentences.zh: 臣雖愚短，守不假器，繡衣所指，冀以清肅。

translations.literal: Though I am dull and limited, I hold office without borrowing authority; where the embroidered robe points, I hope to bring clarity and order.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am dull and limited, I hold office without borrowing authority. Where the embroidered robe of the censor points, I hope to bring clarity and order.

sentences.zh: 若仍更踵前失，或傷善人，則屍祿之責，無所逃罪。

translations.literal: If I again follow previous errors and harm good men, then the charge of holding salary without merit—I cannot escape guilt.
translations.idiomatic: If I again follow previous errors and harm good men, I cannot escape the charge of holding salary without merit.

sentences.zh: 如臣鄙見，請依太和故事，還置司直十人，名隸廷尉，秩以五品，選曆官有稱，心平性正者為之。

translations.literal: In my humble view, please follow the Taihe precedent and restore ten Direct Rectifiers, nominally subordinate to the Court of Justice, ranked at fifth grade, selected from officials with reputation who are even-tempered and upright in nature.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, please follow the Taihe precedent and restore ten Direct Rectifiers, nominally subordinate to the Court of Justice, ranked at fifth grade, selected from officials of reputation who are even-tempered and upright.

sentences.zh: 御史若出糾劾，即移廷尉，令知人數。

translations.literal: If a censor goes out to impeach, he should notify the Court of Justice and inform it of the number of men.
translations.idiomatic: If a censor goes out to impeach, he should notify the Court of Justice of the number of men involved.

sentences.zh: 廷尉遣司直與御史俱發。

translations.literal: The Court of Justice sends Direct Rectifiers to depart together with the censors.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Justice should send Direct Rectifiers to depart together with the censors.

sentences.zh: 所到州郡，分居別館。

translations.literal: At the provinces and commanderies they reach, they lodge in separate quarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the provinces and commanderies they reach, they should lodge in separate quarters.

sentences.zh: 御史檢了，移付司直。

translations.literal: When the censor finishes investigation, he transfers the case to the Direct Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: When the censor finishes investigation, he should transfer the case to the Direct Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 司直覆問事訖，與御史俱還。

translations.literal: When the Direct Rectifier finishes re-examination, he returns together with the censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Direct Rectifier finishes re-examination, he returns together with the censor.

sentences.zh: 中尉彈聞，廷尉科案，一如舊式。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief submits impeachment, the Court of Justice adjudicates the case—all as in the old form.
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief submits impeachment and the Court of Justice adjudicates the case—all as in the old form.

sentences.zh: 庶使獄成罪定，無復稽寬，為惡取敗，不得稱枉。

translations.literal: Thus cases may be closed and guilt fixed, with no further delay or leniency; those who do evil and meet defeat cannot claim injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Thus cases may be closed and guilt fixed without delay or undue leniency, and those who do evil and meet defeat cannot claim injustice.

sentences.zh: 若御史、司直糾劾失實，悉依所斷獄罪之。

translations.literal: If censor or Direct Rectifier impeaches falsely, all are punished according to the sentence for the case they tried.
translations.idiomatic: If censor or Direct Rectifier impeaches falsely, both are punished according to the sentence for the case they tried.

sentences.zh: 聽以所檢，迭相糾發。

translations.literal: They may impeach each other in turn over what each investigated.
translations.idiomatic: They may impeach each other in turn over what each investigated.

sentences.zh: 如二使阿曲，有不盡理，聽罪家詣門下通訴，別加案檢。

translations.literal: If the two envoys bend the law and fail to reach full justice, the convicted family may appeal to the Chancellery, and a separate investigation will be added.
translations.idiomatic: If the two envoys bend the law and fail to reach full justice, the convicted family may appeal to the Chancellery for a separate investigation.

sentences.zh: 如此，則肺石之傍，怨從可息；

translations.literal: In this way, beside the stone of appeal, resentment may cease;
translations.idiomatic: In this way, beside the stone of appeal, resentment may cease;

sentences.zh: 聚棘之下，受罪吞聲者矣。」

translations.literal: Beneath the gathered thorns, those who suffer punishment and swallow their voices are many."
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the gathered thorns, those who suffer punishment in silence would be many."

sentences.zh: 詔從之，復置司直。

translations.literal: An edict followed his proposal and Direct Rectifiers were restored.
translations.idiomatic: An edict adopted his proposal and Direct Rectifiers were restored.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮死，帝召道穆，付赦書，令宣於外，謂曰：「今當得精選御史矣。」

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, the emperor summoned Daomu, handed him the amnesty edict, and ordered him to proclaim it abroad, saying, "Now we can carefully select censors."
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, the emperor summoned Daomu, handed him the amnesty edict, and ordered him to proclaim it abroad, saying, "Now we can carefully select censors."

sentences.zh: 先是，榮等常欲以其親党為御史，故有此詔。

translations.literal: Earlier Rong and others had often wished to appoint their own partisans as censors; therefore this edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Rong and others had often wished to appoint their own partisans as censors, and therefore this edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃世隆等戰于大夏門北，道穆受詔督戰。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Shilong and others fought north of the Daxia Gate, Daomu received an edict to supervise the battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Shilong and others fought north of the Daxia Gate, Daomu received an edict to supervise the battle.

sentences.zh: 又贊成太府卿李苗斷橋之計，世隆等於是北遁。

translations.literal: He also approved Grand Steward Li Miao's plan to break the bridge, and Shilong and others then fled north.
translations.idiomatic: He also approved Grand Steward Li Miao's plan to break the bridge, and Shilong and others fled north.

sentences.zh: 加衛將軍、大都督，兼尚書右僕射、南道大行台。

translations.literal: He was additionally made General of the Guard, Grand Commander, and concurrently Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Southern Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed General of the Guard and Grand Commander, and concurrently Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and commander of the Southern Route Grand Mobile Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時雖外托征蠻，而帝恐北軍不利，欲為南巡之計。

translations.literal: At the time, though outwardly campaigning against the barbarians was the pretext, the emperor feared the northern army would fare badly and wished to plan a southern tour.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, though a campaign against the barbarians was the outward pretext, the emperor feared the northern army would fare badly and planned a southern tour.

sentences.zh: 未發，會爾硃兆入洛，道穆慮禍，託病去官。

translations.literal: Before setting out, Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang; Daomu feared disaster, pleaded illness, and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could set out, Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang. Daomu feared disaster, pleaded illness, and left office.

sentences.zh: 世隆以其忠於前朝，遂害之。

translations.literal: Shilong, because Daomu had been loyal to the former court, then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong killed him because he had been loyal to the former court.

sentences.zh: 太昌中，贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In Taichang he was posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Full Honors, and Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Taichang he was posthumously granted the titles General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Full Honors, and Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 子士鏡襲爵，為北豫州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Shijing inherited the title and became Governor of Beiyuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shijing inherited the title and became Governor of North Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 道穆兄謙之。

translations.literal: Daomu's elder brother Qianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Daomu's elder brother Qianzhi.

sentences.zh: 謙之字道讓，少事後母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Qianzhi's courtesy name was Daorang; from youth he served his stepmother and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi's courtesy name was Daorang. From youth he served his stepmother and was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 專意經史，天文、算曆、圖緯之書，多所該涉。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to the classics and histories and ranged widely through books on astronomy, calendrics, and apocryphal charts.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to the classics and histories and ranged widely through books on astronomy, calendrics, and apocryphal charts.

sentences.zh: 好文章，留心《老》、《易》。

translations.literal: He loved literary composition and attended closely to the Laozi and the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He loved literary composition and attended closely to the Laozi and the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，行河陰令。

translations.literal: In Xiaochang he acted as Magistrate of Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaochang he acted as Magistrate of Heyin.

sentences.zh: 先是有人囊盛瓦礫，指作錢物，詐市人馬，因而逃去。

translations.literal: Earlier someone had bagged rubble and passed it off as money and goods, swindled people out of horses, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier someone had bagged rubble and passed it off as money and goods, swindled people out of horses, and fled.

sentences.zh: 詔令追捕，必得以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered pursuit and capture, with report required.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the culprits be pursued and captured and the result reported.

sentences.zh: 謙之乃偽枷一囚，立于馬市，宣言是前詐市馬賊，今欲刑之。

translations.literal: Qianzhi then falsely put a prisoner in the cangue and set him in the horse market, proclaiming that this was the earlier swindler of horses and that he would now be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi then put a prisoner in a false cangue and set him in the horse market, proclaiming that this was the earlier swindler and that he would now be punished.

sentences.zh: 密遣腹心，察市中私議者。

translations.literal: Secretly he sent trusted men to observe those privately discussing matters in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly he sent trusted men to observe those privately discussing matters in the market.

sentences.zh: 有二人相見，忻然曰：「無復憂矣！」

translations.literal: Two men met and said with delight, "No more worry!"
translations.idiomatic: Two men met and said with delight, "No more worry!"

sentences.zh: 執送案問，悉獲其黨。

translations.literal: They were seized and interrogated, and the whole gang was captured.
translations.idiomatic: They were seized and interrogated, and the whole gang was captured.

sentences.zh: 並出前後盜處，失物之家，各得其本物，具以狀告。

translations.literal: They also revealed all their earlier thefts; households that had lost goods each recovered their original property, and full reports were made.
translations.idiomatic: They also revealed all their earlier thefts. Households that had lost goods recovered their property, and full reports were made.

sentences.zh: 尋正河陰令。

translations.literal: Soon he was formally appointed Magistrate of Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was formally appointed Magistrate of Heyin.

sentences.zh: 在縣二年，損益政體，多為故事。

translations.literal: In two years in the county he improved and adjusted administrative practice, much of which became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In two years in the county he improved administrative practice, much of which became precedent.

sentences.zh: 時道穆為御史，亦有能名，世美其父子兄弟並著當官之稱。

translations.literal: At the time Daomu was a censor and also had a reputation for ability; the age praised father, sons, and brothers alike for their fame in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Daomu was a censor and also had a reputation for ability. The age praised the father, sons, and brothers alike for their fame in office.

sentences.zh: 舊制，二縣令得面陳得失。

translations.literal: By old regulation, the two county magistrates could state gains and losses face to face.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation, the two county magistrates could state gains and losses directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時佞幸之輩，惡其有所發聞，遂共奏罷。

translations.literal: At the time the faction of favorites hated that matters might be exposed and jointly memorialized to abolish the practice.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the faction of favorites hated that matters might be exposed and jointly memorialized to abolish the practice.

sentences.zh: 謙之乃上疏曰：「臣以無庸，謬宰神邑，實思奉法不撓，稱是官方。

translations.literal: Qianzhi then submitted a memorial, saying, "I, worthless as I am, have wrongly been put in charge of the sacred capital; I truly wish to uphold the law without bending and fit the measure of official duty.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi then submitted a memorial: "I, worthless as I am, have wrongly been put in charge of the sacred capital. I truly wish to uphold the law without bending and meet the measure of official duty.

sentences.zh: 酬朝廷無貲之恩，盡人臣守器之節。

translations.literal: To repay the court's grace without asking payment, and fulfill a minister's duty to guard his charge.
translations.idiomatic: To repay the court's grace and fulfill a minister's duty to guard his charge.

sentences.zh: 但豪家支屬，戚裏親媾，縲絏所及，舉目多是。

translations.literal: But among powerful families' branches, in-law connections, and kin by marriage, those touched by bonds and fetters are everywhere one looks.
translations.idiomatic: But among powerful families' branches and in-law connections, those touched by bonds and fetters are everywhere one looks.

sentences.zh: 皆有盜憎之色，咸起惡上之心。

translations.literal: All show the look of thieves who hate authority and all raise hearts of hostility toward superiors.
translations.idiomatic: All show the look of thieves who hate authority and raise hearts of hostility toward superiors.

sentences.zh: 縣令輕弱，何能克濟？

translations.literal: The county magistrate is weak—how can he succeed?
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate is weak—how can he succeed?

sentences.zh: 先帝昔發明詔，得使面陳所懷。

translations.literal: The late emperor once issued a clear edict allowing one to state one's concerns face to face.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor once issued a clear edict allowing magistrates to state their concerns directly.

sentences.zh: 臣亡父先臣崇之為洛陽令，常得入奏是非，所以朝貴斂手，無敢幹政。

translations.literal: My late father, former minister Chong, when Magistrate of Luoyang, could often enter and report right and wrong; therefore the court nobles held their hands and dared not interfere in government.
translations.idiomatic: My late father Chong, when Magistrate of Luoyang, could often enter and report right and wrong. Therefore the court nobles held their hands and dared not interfere in government.

sentences.zh: 近年已來，此制遂寢，致使神宰威輕，下情不達。

translations.literal: In recent years this regulation has lapsed, causing the sacred magistrate's authority to grow light and lower sentiments not to reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years this regulation has lapsed, causing the magistrate's authority to grow light and lower sentiments not to reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 今二聖遠遵堯、舜，憲章高祖，愚臣亦望策其駑蹇，少立功名。

translations.literal: Now the two sages far follow Yao and Shun and take Emperor Gaozu as their model; this dull minister also hopes to spur his lame nag and establish some merit.
translations.idiomatic: Now the two sages far follow Yao and Shun and take Emperor Gaozu as their model. This dull minister also hopes to spur his lame nag and establish some merit.

sentences.zh: 乞行新典，更明往制，庶奸豪知禁，頗自屏心。」

translations.literal: I beg that the new regulation be enacted and the former one clarified again, so that powerful wrongdoers may know prohibition and somewhat restrain their hearts."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the new regulation be enacted and the former one clarified again, so that powerful wrongdoers may know prohibition and restrain themselves."

sentences.zh: 詔付外量聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the matter sent out for deliberation and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the matter sent out for deliberation and report.

sentences.zh: 謙之又上疏，以為：「自正光以來，邊城屢擾，命將出師，相繼于路。

translations.literal: Qianzhi again submitted a memorial, holding that "since Zhenguang the border cities had been repeatedly disturbed and generals ordered to campaign had followed one another on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi again submitted a memorial, arguing that "since Zhenguang the border cities had been repeatedly disturbed and generals ordered to campaign had followed one another on the roads.

sentences.zh: 但諸將帥，或非其才，多遣親者，妄稱入募，唯遣奴客充數而已。

translations.literal: But the commanders were often not fit for their posts; many sent relatives, falsely claiming enlistment, and merely dispatched slaves and retainers to fill the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: But the commanders were often unfit for their posts. Many sent relatives, falsely claiming enlistment, and merely dispatched slaves and retainers to fill the numbers.

sentences.zh: 對寇臨敵，略不彎弓。

translations.literal: Facing bandits and meeting the enemy, they scarcely bent a bow.
translations.idiomatic: Facing the enemy, they scarcely bent a bow.

sentences.zh: 則是王爵虛加，征夫多闕，賊虜何可殄除，忠貞何以勸誡也？

translations.literal: Thus noble titles were given in vain, campaign soldiers were widely lacking—how could bandits be exterminated, and how could loyalty and steadfastness be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: Thus noble titles were given in vain and campaign soldiers were widely lacking. How could bandits be exterminated, and how could loyalty be encouraged?

sentences.zh: 且近習侍臣，戚屬朝士，請托官曹，擅作威福。

translations.literal: Moreover close attendants, court ministers, and kin of the dynasty used official bureaus for patronage and arrogated authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover close attendants, court ministers, and kin of the dynasty used official bureaus for patronage and arrogated authority and favor.

sentences.zh: 如有清貞奉法，不為回者，咸共譖毀，橫受罪罰。

translations.literal: If any were pure, upright, and law-abiding and would not bend, all jointly slandered and destroyed them, and they suffered punishment without cause.
translations.idiomatic: If any were pure, upright, and law-abiding and would not bend, all jointly slandered them and they suffered punishment without cause.

sentences.zh: 在朝顧望，誰肯申聞？

translations.literal: At court all looked about—who would dare report?
translations.idiomatic: At court all looked about—who would dare report?

sentences.zh: 蔽上擁下，虧風損政。

translations.literal: They concealed matters from above and shielded those below, harming custom and damaging government.
translations.idiomatic: They concealed matters from above and shielded those below, harming custom and damaging government.

sentences.zh: 使讒諂甘心，忠讜息義。

translations.literal: They made slander and flattery willing, and loyal remonstrance cease its righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: They made slander and flattery willing and loyal remonstrance cease.

sentences.zh: 且頻年以來，多有徵發，人不堪命，動致流離。

translations.literal: Moreover in recent years there have been many levies and drafts; people cannot bear the burden and constantly flee and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover in recent years there have been many levies and drafts. People cannot bear the burden and constantly flee and scatter.

sentences.zh: 苟保妻子，競逃王役，不復顧其桑井，憚此刑書。

translations.literal: To preserve wife and children they compete to flee royal service, no longer caring for their homes and fields, fearing the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: To preserve wife and children they compete to flee royal service, no longer caring for their homes and fields, fearing the penal code.

sentences.zh: 正由還有必困之理，歸無自安之路。

translations.literal: This is precisely because return brings certain hardship and there is no path to security upon coming back.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely because return brings certain hardship and there is no path to security upon coming back.

sentences.zh: 若聽歸其本業，徭役微甄，則還者必眾，墾田增辟，數年之後，大獲課入。

translations.literal: If they were allowed to return to their original occupations and corvée were lightly assessed, returners would surely be many, reclaimed fields would increase, and after several years tax revenue would greatly grow.
translations.idiomatic: If they were allowed to return to their original occupations and corvée were lightly assessed, returners would surely be many, reclaimed fields would increase, and after several years tax revenue would greatly grow.

sentences.zh: 今不務以理還之，但欲嚴符切勒，恐數年之後，走者更多。

translations.literal: Now, instead of striving to return them by reason, one only wishes to enforce strict orders and tight control—I fear that after several years there will be even more fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Now, instead of striving to return them by reason, the court only wishes to enforce strict orders and tight control. I fear that after several years there will be even more fugitives.

sentences.zh: 故有國有家者，不患人不我歸，唯患政之不立；

translations.literal: Therefore those who have a state or a family do not worry that people will not return to them, but only that government is not established;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore those who have a state or a family do not worry that people will not return to them, but only that government is not established;

sentences.zh: 不恃敵不我攻，唯恃吾不可侮。

translations.literal: they do not rely on enemies not attacking them, but only on their being not to be despised.
translations.idiomatic: they do not rely on enemies not attacking them, but only on their being not to be despised.

sentences.zh: 此乃千載共遵，百王一致。

translations.literal: This is what a thousand ages jointly follow and a hundred kings agree upon.
translations.idiomatic: This is what a thousand ages jointly follow and a hundred kings agree upon.

sentences.zh: 伏願少垂覽察。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will briefly look and examine."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will briefly examine this."

sentences.zh: 靈太后得其疏，以責左右近侍，諸寵要者由是疾之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling received his memorial and rebuked the close attendants; the favored and powerful therefore resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling received his memorial and rebuked the close attendants. The favored and powerful therefore resented him.

sentences.zh: 乃啟太后，雲謙之有學藝，除為國子博士。

translations.literal: They then memorialized the Empress Dowager, saying Qianzhi had learning and skill, and he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: They then memorialized the Empress Dowager, saying Qianzhi had learning and skill, and he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 謙之與袁翻、常景、酈道元、溫子升之徒，或申款舊。

translations.literal: Qianzhi with Yuan Fan, Chang Jing, Li Daoyuan, Wen Zisheng, and others sometimes renewed old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi with Yuan Fan, Chang Jing, Li Daoyuan, Wen Zisheng, and others sometimes renewed old friendships.

sentences.zh: 好施贍恤，言諾無虧。

translations.literal: He loved to give charity and relief; his promises were never broken.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to give charity and relief, and his promises were never broken.

sentences.zh: 居家僮隸，對其兒不撻其父母，生三子便免其一世。

translations.literal: At home with slaves and servants, he would not beat their parents before their children; if a slave bore three sons, one generation was freed.
translations.idiomatic: At home with slaves and servants, he would not beat their parents before their children. If a slave bore three sons, one generation was freed.

sentences.zh: 無愆黥奴婢，常稱：「俱稟人體，如何殘害？」

translations.literal: With faultless branded slaves and maids he often said, "All alike receive human bodies—how can one mutilate and harm them?"
translations.idiomatic: With faultless branded slaves and maids he often said, "All alike receive human bodies—how can one mutilate and harm them?"

sentences.zh: 謙之以父舅氏沮渠蒙遜曾據涼土，國書漏闕，乃修《涼書》十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Because his father's maternal uncle Juqu Mengxun had once held Liang territory and the state records were incomplete, he compiled the History of Liang in ten scrolls, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father's maternal uncle Juqu Mengxun had once held Liang territory and the state records were incomplete, he compiled the History of Liang in ten scrolls, which circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 涼國盛事佛道，為論貶之，稱佛是九流之一家。

translations.literal: The Liang state greatly favored Buddhism and the Way; he wrote a treatise criticizing this, calling the Buddha one school among the Nine Streams.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang state greatly favored Buddhism and the Way. He wrote a treatise criticizing this, calling the Buddha one school among the Nine Streams.

sentences.zh: 當世名流，競以佛理來難，謙之還以佛義對之，竟不能屈。

translations.literal: Famous men of the age competed to challenge him with Buddhist doctrine; Qianzhi answered with Buddhist reasoning in return, and in the end they could not defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: Famous men of the age competed to challenge him with Buddhist doctrine. Qianzhi answered with Buddhist reasoning in return, and in the end they could not defeat him.

sentences.zh: 以時所行曆多未盡善，乃更改元修者撰，為一家之法。

translations.literal: Because the calendar then in use was in many ways not fully good, he revised and compiled a new calendar, making a method of his own school.
translations.idiomatic: Because the calendar then in use was in many ways deficient, he revised and compiled a new calendar, making a method of his own.

sentences.zh: 雖未行於世，識者歎其多能。

translations.literal: Though it was not put into use in the world, those with insight admired his many abilities.
translations.idiomatic: Though it was not put into use, those with insight admired his many abilities.

sentences.zh: 時朝議鑄錢，以謙之為鑄錢都將長者史，乃上表求鑄三銖錢，曰：

translations.literal: At the time the court deliberated on casting coin and made Qianzhi Chief Elder Secretary of the Coin Casting Command; he then submitted a memorial requesting casting of three-zhu coin, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court deliberated on casting coin and made Qianzhi Chief Elder Secretary of the Coin Casting Command. He then submitted a memorial requesting casting of three-zhu coin, saying:

sentences.zh: 蓋錢貨之立，本以通有無，便交易，故錢之輕重，世代不同。

translations.literal: The establishment of money and goods is fundamentally to connect having and not having and facilitate exchange; therefore the weight of coin differs from age to age.
translations.idiomatic: Money was established fundamentally to connect having and not having and facilitate exchange. Therefore the weight of coin differs from age to age.

sentences.zh: 太公為周置九府圜法。

translations.literal: Taigong established for Zhou the Nine Treasuries' round-law system.
translations.idiomatic: Taigong established for Zhou the Nine Treasuries' round-law system of coinage.

sentences.zh: 至景王時，更鑄大錢。

translations.literal: By the time of King Jing, large coin was recast.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of King Jing, large coin was recast.

sentences.zh: 秦兼海內，錢重半兩。

translations.literal: When Qin united the realm within the seas, coin weighed half a liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin united the realm, coin weighed half a liang.

sentences.zh: 漢興，以秦錢重，改鑄榆莢錢。

translations.literal: When Han arose, because Qin coin was heavy, elm-pod coin was recast.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose, because Qin coin was heavy, elm-pod coin was recast.

sentences.zh: 至文帝五年，復為四銖。

translations.literal: By the fifth year of Emperor Wen it was again made four zhu.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth year of Emperor Wen it was again made four zhu.

sentences.zh: 孝武時悉復銷壞，更鑄三銖。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaowu's time all was melted down again and recast as three zhu.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wu's time all was melted down again and recast as three zhu.

sentences.zh: 至無狩中，變為五銖。

translations.literal: By the Yuan Shou era it was changed to five zhu.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yuan Shou era it was changed to five zhu.

sentences.zh: 又造赤仄之錢，以一當五。

translations.literal: Red slant coin was also made, one counting as five.
translations.idiomatic: Red slant coin was also made, one counting as five.

sentences.zh: 王莽攝政，錢有六等：大錢重十二銖，次九銖，次七銖，次五銖，次三銖，次一銖。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang held regency, coin had six grades: large coin weighing twelve zhu, then nine, then seven, then five, then three, then one zhu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang held regency, coin had six grades: large coin weighing twelve zhu, then nine, seven, five, three, and one zhu.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝罷五銖錢，至明帝復立。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei abolished five-zhu coin; by Emperor Ming it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei abolished five-zhu coin; by Emperor Ming it was restored.

sentences.zh: 孫權江左鑄大錢，一當五百。

translations.literal: Sun Quan in the lands east of the river cast large coin, one counting as five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan in the lands east of the river cast large coin, one counting as five hundred.

sentences.zh: 權赤烏年，復鑄大錢，一當千。

translations.literal: In Sun Quan's Chiwu era large coin was again cast, one counting as a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Sun Quan's Chiwu era large coin was again cast, one counting as a thousand.

sentences.zh: 輕重大小，莫不隨時而變。

translations.literal: Light and heavy, large and small—all changed with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Light and heavy, large and small—all changed with the times.

sentences.zh: 竊以食貨之要，八政為首，聚財之貴，詒訓典文。

translations.literal: I consider that among the essentials of food and goods, the eight policies put this first; the preciousness of gathering wealth is handed down in canonical texts.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that among the essentials of food and goods, the eight policies put this first, and the preciousness of gathering wealth is handed down in canonical texts.

sentences.zh: 是以昔之帝王，乘天地之饒，禦海內之富，莫不腐紅粟於太倉，藏朽貫於泉府。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperors of old, riding the abundance of Heaven and Earth and controlling the wealth within the seas, all rotted red grain in the Grand Storehouse and hoarded worn strings of cash in the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the emperors of old, riding the abundance of Heaven and Earth and controlling the wealth within the seas, all filled the Grand Storehouse with grain and hoarded strings of cash in the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 儲畜既盈，人無困弊，可以甯謐四海，如身使臂者矣。

translations.literal: When stores were full and people free from hardship, they could pacify the four seas, using the realm as one uses arm from body.
translations.idiomatic: When stores were full and people free from hardship, they could pacify the four seas, directing the realm as one uses an arm from the body.

sentences.zh: 昔漢之孝武，地廣財饒，外事四戎，遂虛國用。

translations.literal: Formerly Han's Emperor Xiaowu, with broad territory and rich resources, had foreign affairs with the four barbarians and thus emptied state expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han's Emperor Wu, with broad territory and rich resources, had foreign affairs with the four barbarians and thus emptied state expenditure.

sentences.zh: 於是草茅之臣，出財助邊；

translations.literal: Then men of humble thatch contributed wealth to aid the borders;
translations.idiomatic: Then men of humble thatch contributed wealth to aid the borders;

sentences.zh: 興利之計，納稅廟堂。

translations.literal: profit-seeking plans were brought into the ancestral hall as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: profit-seeking plans were brought into the ancestral hall as tribute.

sentences.zh: 市列榷酒之官，邑有告緡之令。

translations.literal: In markets were placed wine-monopoly officers; in districts were orders to report hidden wealth.
translations.idiomatic: In markets were placed wine-monopoly officers; in districts were orders to report hidden wealth.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵既興，錢弊屢改，少府遂豐，上林饒積。

translations.literal: When salt and iron monopolies arose and coin was repeatedly changed, the Privy Treasury grew rich and Shanglin Park abounded in stores.
translations.idiomatic: When salt and iron monopolies arose and coin was repeatedly changed, the Privy Treasury grew rich and Shanglin Park abounded in stores.

sentences.zh: 外辟百蠻，內不增賦者，皆計利之由也。

translations.literal: Opening the hundred barbarians abroad without increasing levies at home—all came from calculating profit.
translations.idiomatic: Opening the hundred barbarians abroad without increasing levies at home—all came from calculating profit.

sentences.zh: 今群妖未息，四郊多壘，徵稅既煩，千金日費，倉儲漸耗，財用將竭，誠楊氏獻稅之秋，桑兒言利之日。

translations.literal: Now the many rebels are not yet stilled, the four suburbs are full of fortifications, levies are already burdensome, a thousand gold is spent daily, storehouses are gradually depleted and funds nearly exhausted—truly this is the season when the Yang clan offered tribute and the day when Sang Er spoke of profit.
translations.idiomatic: Now rebels are not yet stilled, the four suburbs are full of fortifications, levies are burdensome, a thousand gold is spent daily, storehouses are depleted and funds nearly exhausted—truly this is the season when the Yang clan offered tribute and the day when Sang Er spoke of profit.

sentences.zh: 夫以西京之盛，錢猶屢改，並行大小，子母相權。

translations.literal: Even in the splendor of the Western Capital, coin was repeatedly changed, large and small circulated together, parent and child coins balancing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the splendor of the Western Capital, coin was repeatedly changed, large and small circulated together, parent and child coins balancing each other.

sentences.zh: 況今寇難未除，州郡淪敗，人物凋零，軍國用少。

translations.literal: How much more now, when bandit troubles are not yet removed, provinces and commanderies have fallen, people are withering away, and military and state expenditure is small.
translations.idiomatic: How much more now, when bandit troubles are not yet removed, provinces and commanderies have fallen, people are withering away, and military and state funds are scarce.

sentences.zh: 別鑄小錢，可以富益，何損於政，何妨於人也？

translations.literal: Separately casting small coin can enrich and benefit—what harm to government, what obstacle to the people?
translations.idiomatic: Separately casting small coin can enrich and benefit—what harm to government, what obstacle to the people?

sentences.zh: 且政興不以錢大，政衰不以錢小，唯貴公私得所，政化無虧，既行之于古，亦宜效之於今矣。

translations.literal: Moreover government does not rise because coin is large nor decline because coin is small; what matters is that public and private find their proper place and government and transformation suffer no loss. Since this was done in antiquity, it should also be imitated today.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover government does not rise because coin is large nor decline because coin is small. What matters is that public and private find their proper place and government suffers no loss. Since this was done in antiquity, it should also be imitated today.

sentences.zh: 昔禹遭大水，以曆山之金鑄錢，救人之困；

translations.literal: Formerly Yu met the great flood and cast coin from the gold of Li Mountain to relieve people's distress;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Yu met the great flood and cast coin from the gold of Li Mountain to relieve people's distress;

sentences.zh: 湯遭大旱，以莊山之金鑄錢，贖人之賣子者。

translations.literal: Tang met great drought and cast coin from the gold of Zhuang Mountain to redeem those who had sold their children.
translations.idiomatic: Tang met great drought and cast coin from the gold of Zhuang Mountain to redeem those who had sold their children.

sentences.zh: 今百姓窮悴，甚於曩日，欽明之主，豈得垂拱而觀之哉？

translations.literal: Now the common people are destitute and worn, worse than in former days—can a reverent and clear-sighted ruler fold his hands and merely watch?
translations.idiomatic: Now the common people are destitute and worn, worse than in former days. Can a reverent and clear-sighted ruler fold his hands and merely watch?

sentences.zh: 臣今此鑄，以濟交乏，五銖之錢，任使並用，行之無損，國得其益。

translations.literal: My casting now is to relieve mutual want; five-zhu coin may be used as one sees fit together with it—put into practice it will do no harm and the state will gain benefit.
translations.idiomatic: My proposal to cast coin now is to relieve mutual want. Five-zhu coin may continue in use alongside it—put into practice it will do no harm and the state will gain benefit.

sentences.zh: 詔將從之。

translations.literal: An edict was about to follow his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was about to adopt his proposal.

sentences.zh: 事未就，會卒。

translations.literal: The matter was not completed when he happened to die.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was not completed when he died.

sentences.zh: 初，謙之弟道穆，正光中為御史，糾相州刺史李世哲事，大相挫辱，其家恆以為憾。

translations.literal: At first Qianzhi's younger brother Daomu, in Zhenguang as a censor, impeached Inspector of Xiangzhou Li Shizhe and greatly humiliated him; the Li family always resented this.
translations.idiomatic: At first Qianzhi's younger brother Daomu, serving as censor during Zhenguang, impeached Inspector of Xiang Province Li Shizhe and greatly humiliated him. The Li family always resented this.

sentences.zh: 至是世哲弟神軌為靈太后深所寵任，會謙之家僮訴良，神軌左右之，入諷尚書，判禁謙之于廷尉。

translations.literal: At this time Shizhe's younger brother Shengui was deeply favored and trusted by Empress Dowager Ling; it happened that Qianzhi's household slave sued Liang, and Shengui sided with him, went in and hinted to the Secretariat, which judged to imprison Qianzhi in the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Shizhe's younger brother Shengui was deeply favored by Empress Dowager Ling. When Qianzhi's household slave sued Liang, Shengui sided with him, hinted to the Secretariat, and Qianzhi was imprisoned in the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時將赦，神軌乃啟靈太后，發詔於獄賜死。

translations.literal: When an amnesty was about to be issued, Shengui memorialized the Empress Dowager and an edict was sent to the prison granting death.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty was about to be issued, Shengui memorialized the Empress Dowager and an edict was sent to the prison ordering Qianzhi's death.

sentences.zh: 朝士莫不哀之。

translations.literal: No court gentleman failed to mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: Every court gentleman mourned him.

sentences.zh: 所著文章百餘篇，別有集錄。

translations.literal: He wrote more than a hundred essays, and there is a separate collected record.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than a hundred essays, collected in a separate volume.

sentences.zh: 永安中，贈營州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: In Yong'an he was posthumously granted Governor of Yingzhou, with posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an he was posthumously granted the title Governor of Ying Province, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 又除一子出身，以明冤屈。

translations.literal: One son was also granted initial appointment to clarify the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: One son was also granted initial appointment to acknowledge the injustice.

sentences.zh: 謙之弟謹之，字道修。

translations.literal: Qianzhi's younger brother Jinzhi's courtesy name was Daoxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi's younger brother Jinzhi's courtesy name was Daoxiu.

sentences.zh: 父崇既還本姓，以謹之繼沮渠氏。

translations.literal: When father Chong had restored his original surname, Jinzhi was made to succeed the Juqu clan.
translations.idiomatic: When their father Chong restored his original surname, Jinzhi succeeded to the Juqu clan line.

sentences.zh: 綦俊，字剽顯，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Qi Jun, courtesy name Piaoxian, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jun, courtesy name Piaoxian, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 其先居代。

translations.literal: His ancestors lived in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had lived in Dai.

sentences.zh: 俊孝莊時仕，累遷為滄州刺史，甚為吏人畏悅。

translations.literal: Jun served in Xiaozhuang's time, was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Cangzhou, and was greatly feared and liked by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Jun served during Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, was promoted to Governor of Cang Province, and was greatly feared and liked by officials and people.

sentences.zh: 尋除太僕卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Master of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Grand Master of the Stud.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃世隆等誅，齊神武召文武百司，下及士庶，議所立。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Shilong and others were executed, Gao Huan of Qi summoned civil and military officials from the hundred bureaus down to gentry and commoners to deliberate whom to establish.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Shilong and others were executed, Gao Huan of Qi summoned civil and military officials and commoners alike to deliberate whom to establish as emperor.

sentences.zh: 莫有應者。

translations.literal: No one responded.
translations.idiomatic: No one responded.

sentences.zh: 俊避席曰：「廣陵王雖為爾硃扶戴，當今之聖主也。」

translations.literal: Jun left his seat and said, "Prince of Guangling, though raised up by Erzhu, is the sage ruler of the present age."
translations.idiomatic: Jun left his seat and said, "Prince of Guangling, though raised up by Erzhu, is the sage ruler of the present age."

sentences.zh: 神武將從之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan was about to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was about to follow this advice.

sentences.zh: 時黃門崔甗議不同，高乾、魏蘭根等固執甗言，遂立孝武帝。

translations.literal: At the time Yellow Gate Cui Yan held a different view; Gao Gan, Wei Langen, and others firmly upheld Yan's words, and Emperor Xiaowu was therefore established.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yellow Gate Cui Yan held a different view. Gao Gan, Wei Langen, and others firmly upheld Yan's words, and Emperor Xiaowu was therefore established.

sentences.zh: 及帝入關，神武深思俊言，常以為恨。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered Guan, Gao Huan deeply reflected on Jun's words and always regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled into Guan, Gao Huan deeply reflected on Jun's words and always regretted not following them.

sentences.zh: 尋除御史中尉，于路與僕射賈顯度相逢，顯度恃勳貴，排俊騶列倒，俊忿見於色，自入奏之。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Censor-in-Chief; on the road he met Vice Director Jia Xiandu; Xiandu, relying on merit and rank, pushed Jun's outriders' line over; Jun's anger showed on his face, and he went in himself to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Censor-in-Chief. On the road he met Vice Director Jia Xiandu, who, relying on merit and rank, pushed Jun's outriders' line aside. Jun's anger showed on his face, and he memorialized the incident himself.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍、左光祿大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Regular Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Full Honors.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally appointed Regular Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Full Honors.

sentences.zh: 俊佞巧，能候當塗，斛斯椿、賀拔勝皆與友善。

translations.literal: Jun was sycophantic and crafty, able to watch those in power; Husi Chun and Heba Sheng were all friendly with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was sycophantic and crafty, skilled at watching those in power. Husi Chun and Heba Sheng were all friendly with him.

sentences.zh: 性多詐，賀拔勝出鎮荊州，過俊別，因辭俊母。

translations.literal: By nature he was much given to deceit; when Heba Sheng went out to garrison Jingzhou, he passed Jun's home to take leave and therefore paid respects to Jun's mother.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was much given to deceit. When Heba Sheng went out to garrison Jing Province, he stopped at Jun's home to take leave and paid respects to Jun's mother.

sentences.zh: 俊故見敗氈弊被，勝更遺之錢物。

translations.literal: Jun deliberately showed torn felt and worn bedding; Sheng furthermore sent him money and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Jun deliberately showed torn felt and worn bedding, and Sheng sent him money and goods.

sentences.zh: 後兼吏部尚書，復為滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was concurrently Minister of Personnel and again became Governor of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served concurrently as Minister of Personnel and again became Governor of Cang Province.

sentences.zh: 徵還，兼中尉，章武縣伯。

translations.literal: Summoned back, he was concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Baron of Zhangwu County.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned back, he served concurrently as Censor-in-Chief and was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhangwu County.

sentences.zh: 尋除殷州刺史，薨于州。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Yinzhou and died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Governor of Yin Province and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈司空公，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Duke of the Minister of Works, with posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Duke of the Minister of Works, with the posthumous name Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 子洪實，字巨正，位尚書左右郎、魏郡邑中正。

translations.literal: His son Hongshi, courtesy name Juzheng, held the posts of Left and Right Lang of the Secretariat and Rectifier of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongshi, courtesy name Juzheng, served as Left and Right Lang of the Secretariat and Rectifier of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 嗜酒好色，無行檢，卒。

translations.literal: He was fond of wine and women, without moral restraint, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of wine and women, without moral restraint, and died.

sentences.zh: 山偉，字仲才，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Shan Wei, courtesy name Zhongcai, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Wei, courtesy name Zhongcai, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 其先居代。

translations.literal: His ancestors lived in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had lived in Dai.

sentences.zh: 祖強，美容貌，身長八尺五寸，工騎射，彎弓五石，為奏事中散。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiang had a handsome appearance, stood eight feet five inches, was skilled at mounted archery, drew a bow of five shi, and was Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiang was handsome, stood eight feet five inches, was skilled at mounted archery, drew a bow of five shi, and served as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 從獻文獵方山，有兩狐起於御前，詔強射之，百步內，二狐俱獲。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Xianwen on a hunt at Mount Fang, two foxes rose before the imperial carriage; an edict ordered Qiang to shoot them, and within a hundred paces both foxes were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Xianwen on a hunt at Mount Fang, two foxes rose before the imperial carriage. An edict ordered Qiang to shoot them, and within a hundred paces both foxes were taken.

sentences.zh: 位內行長。

translations.literal: He held the post of Director of Inner Conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of Director of Inner Conduct.

sentences.zh: 父幼之，位金明太守。

translations.literal: His father Youzhi held the post of Grand Administrator of Jinming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Youzhi served as Grand Administrator of Jinming.

sentences.zh: 偉涉獵文史，孝明初，元匡為御史中尉，以偉兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Wei ranged through literature and history; at the beginning of Xiaoming, Yuan Kuang was Censor-in-Chief and made Wei concurrently Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ranged through literature and history. At the beginning of Xiaoming, Yuan Kuang was Censor-in-Chief and made Wei concurrently Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 入台五日，便遇正會，偉司神武門。

translations.literal: Five days after entering the censorate he met a regular court session; Wei was on duty at the Shenwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Five days after entering the censorate he met a regular court session. Wei was on duty at the Shenwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 其妻從叔為羽林隊主，撾直長於殿門，偉即劾奏。

translations.literal: His wife's uncle by marriage was chief of a Feathered Forest squad; he beat a duty officer at the palace gate, and Wei immediately impeached and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's uncle by marriage was chief of a Feathered Forest squad. He beat a duty officer at the palace gate, and Wei immediately impeached him.

sentences.zh: 匡善之，俄然奏正，帖國子助教，遷員外郎、廷尉評。

translations.literal: Kuang approved; soon he was formally appointed, posted as Assistant Erudite of the Imperial Academy, and transferred to Supernumerary Lang and Reviewer of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang approved. Soon Wei was formally appointed Assistant Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then transferred to Supernumerary Lang and Reviewer of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時天下無事，進仕路難，代遷之人，多不沾預。

translations.literal: At the time the realm was at peace, the path to office was difficult, and people transferred from Dai were mostly not included.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the realm was at peace, the path to office was difficult, and people transferred from Dai were mostly excluded.

sentences.zh: 及六鎮、隴西二方起逆，領軍元叉欲用代來寒人為傳詔，以慰悅之，而牧守子孫投狀求者百餘人。

translations.literal: When the Six Garrisons and Longxi regions both rose in rebellion, Army Supervisor Yuan Cha wished to use poor men from Dai as edict-bearers to console and please them, but more than a hundred descendants of regional governors submitted petitions seeking appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Garrisons and Longxi regions both rose in rebellion, Army Supervisor Yuan Cha wished to use poor men from Dai as edict-bearers to console them, but more than a hundred descendants of regional governors submitted petitions seeking appointment.

sentences.zh: 叉因奏立勳附隊，令各依資出身。

translations.literal: Cha therefore memorialized to establish a Merit Attachment Corps, letting each enter office according to qualification.
translations.idiomatic: Cha therefore memorialized to establish a Merit Attachment Corps, letting each enter office according to qualification.

sentences.zh: 自是北人，悉被收敘。

translations.literal: From this all northerners were enrolled and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: From this all northerners were enrolled and promoted.

sentences.zh: 偉遂奏記，贊叉德美。

translations.literal: Wei then submitted a letter praising Cha's virtue and excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Wei then submitted a letter praising Cha's virtue and excellence.

sentences.zh: 叉素不識偉，訪侍中安豐王延明、黃門郎元順，順等因是稱薦之。

translations.literal: Cha had never known Wei and inquired of Palace Attendant Prince of Anfeng Yanming and Yellow Gate Gentleman Yuan Shun; Shun and others therefore praised and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Cha had never known Wei and inquired of Palace Attendant Prince of Anfeng Yanming and Yellow Gate Gentleman Yuan Shun. Shun and others therefore praised and recommended him.

sentences.zh: 叉令僕射元欽引偉兼尚書二千石郎，後正名士郎，修起居注。

translations.literal: Cha had Vice Director Yuan Qin recruit Wei as concurrently Lang of the Secretariat at two-thousand-shi rank; later he was formally appointed Lang of Notable Names and edited the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: Cha had Vice Director Yuan Qin recruit Wei as concurrently a two-thousand-shi secretary in the Secretariat. Later he was formally appointed Lang of Notable Names and edited the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 僕射元順領選，表薦為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Vice Director Yuan Shun oversaw selection and memorialized recommending him as Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan Shun oversaw selection and recommended him as Grand Master of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮之害朝士，偉時守直，故免禍。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong harmed court gentlemen, Wei was then on duty and upright, and therefore escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong slaughtered court gentlemen, Wei was on duty and upheld rectitude, and therefore escaped disaster.

sentences.zh: 及孝莊入宮，仍除偉給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhuang entered the palace, Wei was still appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhuang entered the palace, Wei was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 先是偉與儀曹郎袁升、屯田郎李延考、外兵郎李奐、三公郎王延業方駕而行，偉少居後。

translations.literal: Earlier Wei was riding in the same carriage with Ritual Section Lang Yuan Sheng, Colonization Lang Li Yan'kao, External Military Lang Li Huan, and Three Dukes Lang Wang Yanye; Wei was slightly behind.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wei was riding with Ritual Section Lang Yuan Sheng, Colonization Lang Li Yan'kao, External Military Lang Li Huan, and Three Dukes Lang Wang Yanye. Wei was slightly behind.

sentences.zh: 路逢一尼，望之歎曰：「此輩緣業，同日而死。」

translations.literal: On the road they met a nun who looked at them and sighed, "These men's karmic lot—on the same day they will die."
translations.idiomatic: On the road they met a nun who looked at them and sighed, "These men's karmic lot binds them to die on the same day."

sentences.zh: 謂偉曰：「君方近天子，當作好官。」

translations.literal: She said to Wei, "You will soon be near the Son of Heaven—you should become a good official."
translations.idiomatic: She said to Wei, "You will soon be near the Son of Heaven—you should become a good official."

sentences.zh: 而升等四人皆于河陰遇害，果如其言。

translations.literal: Sheng and the other four all met harm at Heyin, exactly as she had said.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and the other four all met harm at Heyin, exactly as she had said.

sentences.zh: 俄領著作郎，節閔帝立，除秘書監，仍著作。

translations.literal: Soon he headed the Compiler's Office; when Emperor Jiemin was established, he was appointed Director of the Secretariat Library and still compiled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he headed the Compiler's Office. When Emperor Jiemin was established, he was appointed Director of the Secretariat Library while still compiling.

sentences.zh: 初，爾硃兆入洛，官守奔散，國史典書高法顯密埋史書，故不遺落。

translations.literal: At first when Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, officials fled and scattered; Keeper of the National History Gao Faxian secretly buried the historical books, so they were not lost.
translations.idiomatic: At first when Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, officials fled and scattered. Keeper of the National History Gao Faxian secretly buried the historical books, so they were not lost.

sentences.zh: 偉自以為功，訴求爵賞。

translations.literal: Wei considered this his own merit and petitioned for title and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Wei considered this his own merit and petitioned for title and reward.

sentences.zh: 偉挾附世隆，遂封東阿縣伯，而法顯止獲男爵。

translations.literal: Wei relied on attachment to Shilong and was therefore enfeoffed as Baron of Dong'a County, while Faxian received only a baron's title.
translations.idiomatic: Wei relied on attachment to Shilong and was enfeoffed as Baron of Dong'a County, while Faxian received only a baron's title.

sentences.zh: 偉尋進侍中。

translations.literal: Wei soon advanced to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wei soon advanced to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，除衛大將軍，中書令，監起居。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing he was appointed Grand General of the Guard, Director of the Secretariat, and overseer of the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaojing he was appointed Grand General of the Guard, Director of the Secretariat, and overseer of the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 後以本官復領著作，卒官。

translations.literal: Later, retaining his original office, he again headed compilation and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, retaining his original office, he again headed compilation and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、都督、幽州刺史，諡曰文貞公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Full Honors and Grand Marshal's Office, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Youzhou, with posthumous title Duke Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Full Honors and Grand Marshal's Office, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of You Province, with the posthumous name Duke Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 國史自鄧彥海、崔深、崔浩、高允、李彪、崔光以還，諸人相繼撰錄。

translations.literal: Since Deng Yanhai, Cui Shen, Cui Hao, Gao Yun, Li Biao, and Cui Guang, the National History had been compiled in succession by various men.
translations.idiomatic: Since Deng Yanhai, Cui Shen, Cui Hao, Gao Yun, Li Biao, and Cui Guang, the National History had been compiled in succession by various men.

sentences.zh: 綦俊及偉等諂悅上党王天穆及爾硃世隆，以為國書正應代人修緝，不宜委之餘人，是以綦、偉等更主大籍。

translations.literal: Qi Jun and Wei and others flattered Prince of Shangdang Tianmu and Erzhu Shilong, holding that the state annals should properly be edited by men of Dai and not entrusted to others; therefore Qi, Wei, and others again took charge of the great records.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jun, Wei, and others flattered Prince of Shangdang Tianmu and Erzhu Shilong, holding that the state annals should be edited by men of Dai and not entrusted to others. Therefore Qi, Wei, and others again took charge of the great records.

sentences.zh: 守舊而已，初無述著，故自崔鴻死後，迄終偉身，二十許載，時事蕩然，萬不記一。

translations.literal: They merely kept the old material and at first wrote nothing new; therefore from Cui Hong's death until Wei's end, some twenty years, current events were utterly lost—not one in ten thousand was recorded.
translations.idiomatic: They merely kept the old material and wrote nothing new. Therefore from Cui Hong's death until Wei's end, some twenty years, current events were utterly lost—not one in ten thousand was recorded.

sentences.zh: 後人執筆，無所憑據，史之遺闕，偉之由也。

translations.literal: Later men who took up the brush had nothing to rely on; the gaps in history were Wei's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Later historians had nothing to rely on. The gaps in history were Wei's doing.

sentences.zh: 外示沈厚，內實矯競。

translations.literal: Outwardly he showed depth and weight; inwardly he was in fact pretentious and competitive.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he showed depth and weight; inwardly he was pretentious and competitive.

sentences.zh: 與綦俊少甚相得，晚以名位之間，遂若水火。

translations.literal: With Qi Jun he was very close in youth; in later years, over rank and position, they became like fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: With Qi Jun he was very close in youth. In later years, over rank and position, they became like fire and water.

sentences.zh: 與宇文忠之之徒代人為党，時賢畏惡之。

translations.literal: With Yuwen Zhongzhi and others he formed a faction of men from Dai; men of talent of the time feared and despised them.
translations.idiomatic: With Yuwen Zhongzhi and others he formed a faction of men from Dai. Men of talent of the time feared and despised them.

sentences.zh: 而愛尚文史，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: Yet he loved and honored literature and history, and grew more devoted in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved literature and history, and grew more devoted in old age.

sentences.zh: 偉弟少亡，偉撫寡訓孤，同居二十餘載，恩義甚篤。

translations.literal: Wei's younger brother died young; Wei raised the widow and instructed the orphan, living together more than twenty years with deep kindness and duty.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's younger brother died young. Wei raised the widow and instructed the orphan, living together more than twenty years with deep kindness and duty.

sentences.zh: 不營產業，身亡之後，賣宅營葬，妻女不免飄泊，士友歎湣之。

translations.literal: He did not build up property; after his death his house was sold to arrange burial, and wife and daughters could not avoid drifting—scholar friends sighed in pity.
translations.idiomatic: He did not build up property. After his death his house was sold to arrange burial, and his wife and daughters were left adrift—scholar friends sighed in pity.

sentences.zh: 長子昂襲爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ang inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 宇文忠之，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuwen Zhongzhi was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhongzhi was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 其先南單于之遠屬，世據東部，後居代都。

translations.literal: His ancestors were distant kin of the Southern Chanyu, for generations holding the eastern region, later living at the capital of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were distant kin of the Southern Chanyu, for generations holding the eastern region, later living at the capital of Dai.

sentences.zh: 父侃，卒于書侍御史。

translations.literal: His father Kan died while Attending Censor of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kan died while serving as Attending Censor of Documents.

sentences.zh: 忠之涉獵文史，頗有筆劄，釋褐太學博士。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi ranged through literature and history, had considerable skill with the brush, and upon leaving the hemp became Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi ranged through literature and history and had considerable skill with the brush. Upon entering office he became Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 天平初，除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was appointed Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was appointed Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 裴伯茂與之同省，常侮忽之，以忠之色黑，呼為「黑宇」。

translations.literal: Pei Bomao was in the same bureau and often treated him with contempt; because Zhongzhi's complexion was dark, he called him "Black Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Bomao was in the same bureau and often treated him with contempt. Because Zhongzhi's complexion was dark, he called him "Black Yu."

sentences.zh: 後敕修國史。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered him to revise the National History.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict ordered him to revise the National History.

sentences.zh: 元象初，兼通直散騎常侍，副鄭伯猷，使梁。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he was concurrently Regular Attendant for Direct Communication, deputy to Zheng Boyou on a mission to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he served concurrently as Regular Attendant for Direct Communication, deputy to Zheng Boyou on a mission to Liang.

sentences.zh: 武定初，為尚書右丞，仍修史。
