translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he became Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat and still revised history.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuding he became Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat while still revising history.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以事除名。

translations.literal: Before long, because of an affair he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, because of an affair he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 忠之好榮利。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi loved glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi loved glory and profit.

sentences.zh: 自為中書郎六七年矣，遇尚書省選右丞，預選者皆射策，忠之試焉。

translations.literal: He had been a Secretariat Gentleman for six or seven years when the Secretariat selected a Right Assistant Director; all candidates took the written examination, and Zhongzhi tried it.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a Secretariat Gentleman for six or seven years when the Secretariat selected a Right Assistant Director. All candidates took the written examination, and Zhongzhi tried it.

sentences.zh: 既獲丞職，大為忻滿，志氣囂然，有驕物之色。

translations.literal: Once he obtained the assistant director post he was greatly pleased and satisfied, his spirit arrogant, with a look that scorned others.
translations.idiomatic: Once he obtained the assistant director post he was greatly pleased, his spirit arrogant, with a look that scorned others.

sentences.zh: 識者笑之。

translations.literal: Those with insight laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Those with insight laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 既失官爵，怏怏發疾，卒於君山。

translations.literal: Once he lost office and title he fell ill from resentment and died on Mount Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Once he lost office and title he fell ill from resentment and died on Mount Jun.

sentences.zh: 費穆，字朗興，代人也。

translations.literal: Fei Mu, courtesy name Langxing, was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Mu, courtesy name Langxing, was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 祖于，位商賈二曹令、懷州刺史，賜爵松陽男。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu held the posts of Director of the Two Commerce Bureaus and Governor of Huaizhou, and was granted the title Baron of Songyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu served as Director of the Two Commerce Bureaus and Governor of Huai Province, and was granted the title Baron of Songyang.

sentences.zh: 父萬襲爵，位梁州鎮將，贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Wan inherited the title, held the post of Garrison General of Liangzhou, and was posthumously granted Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wan inherited the title, served as Garrison General of Liang Province, and was posthumously granted the title Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 穆性剛烈，有壯氣，頗涉文史，好尚功名。

translations.literal: Mu's nature was fierce and bold, with a vigorous spirit; he ranged considerably through literature and history and loved to seek merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's nature was fierce and bold, with a vigorous spirit. He ranged considerably through literature and history and loved to seek merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，襲爵，稍遷涇州平西府長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanwu he inherited the title and was gradually promoted to Chief Clerk of Jingzhou's Western Pacification Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xuanwu he inherited the title and was gradually promoted to Chief Clerk of the Western Pacification Headquarters at Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 時刺史皇甫集，靈太后之元舅，恃外戚之親，多為非法。

translations.literal: At the time Inspector Huangfu Ji, the Empress Dowager Ling's eldest maternal uncle, relied on kinship as an external relative and did many illegal things.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Inspector Huangfu Ji, the Empress Dowager Ling's eldest maternal uncle, relied on his kinship with the empress and did many illegal things.

sentences.zh: 穆正色匡諫，集亦憚之。

translations.literal: Mu with stern countenance set aright and remonstrated, and Ji also feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Mu remonstrated with stern countenance, and Ji also feared him.

sentences.zh: 後蠕蠕主婆羅門自涼州歸降，其部眾因饑侵掠邊邑。

translations.literal: Later the Rouran ruler Poluomen submitted from Liangzhou; his tribes, because of hunger, raided border settlements.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Rouran ruler Poluomen submitted from Liang Province. His tribes, driven by hunger, raided border settlements.

sentences.zh: 詔穆銜旨宣慰，莫不款附。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Mu to carry the imperial message and console them; none failed to submit in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Mu to carry the imperial message and console them, and all submitted in good faith.

sentences.zh: 明年復叛，入寇涼州。

translations.literal: The next year they rebelled again and invaded Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they rebelled again and invaded Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 除穆兼尚書右丞、西北道行台，仍為別將，往討之。

translations.literal: Mu was appointed concurrently Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat and Mobile Headquarters of the Northwestern Route, and still as separate commander went to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Mu was appointed concurrently Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat and commander of the Northwestern Route Mobile Headquarters, and as separate commander went to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 穆至涼州，蠕蠕遁走。

translations.literal: When Mu reached Liangzhou, the Rouran fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu reached Liang Province, the Rouran fled.

sentences.zh: 穆謂其所部曰：「夷狄獸心，見敵便走，若不令其破膽，終恐疲於奔命。」

translations.literal: Mu told his troops, "Barbarians have the hearts of beasts—seeing the enemy they flee. If we do not break their courage, we will ultimately wear ourselves out in endless pursuit."
translations.idiomatic: Mu told his troops, "Barbarians have the hearts of beasts—they flee at the sight of the enemy. If we do not break their courage, we will wear ourselves out in endless pursuit."

sentences.zh: 乃簡練精騎，伏於山谷，使羸劣之眾為外營，以誘之。

translations.literal: He then selected and trained elite cavalry, hid them in valleys, and set weak troops as an outer camp to lure them.
translations.idiomatic: He then selected elite cavalry, hid them in the valleys, and set weak troops in an outer camp to lure the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊騎覘見，俄而競至，伏兵奔擊，大破之。

translations.literal: The bandit cavalry saw and soon raced up; the hidden troops charged and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy cavalry spotted the camp and soon raced up. The hidden troops charged and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 及六鎮反叛，穆為別將，隸都督李崇北伐。

translations.literal: When the Six Garrisons rebelled, Mu was a separate commander under Commander-in-Chief Li Chong on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Garrisons rebelled, Mu served as separate commander under Commander-in-Chief Li Chong on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 都督崔暹失利，崇將議班師。

translations.literal: Commander Cui Xuan suffered defeat; Chong was about to discuss withdrawing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Cui Xuan suffered defeat, and Chong was about to discuss withdrawing the army.

sentences.zh: 以朔州是白道之沖，賊之咽喉，若不全，則並、肆危，選將鎮捍，僉議舉穆。

translations.literal: Because Shuozhou was the choke point of the White Road and the bandits' throat—if it were not secured, Bing and Si would be in peril—a general was chosen to garrison and defend it, and all agreed to recommend Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shuo Province was the choke point of the White Road and the rebels' vital passage—if it were not secured, Bing and Si would be in peril—all agreed to recommend Mu to garrison and defend it.

sentences.zh: 崇乃請穆為朔州刺史。

translations.literal: Chong therefore requested Mu as Governor of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chong therefore requested that Mu be appointed Governor of Shuo Province.

sentences.zh: 尋改雲州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Governor of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Governor of Yun Province.

sentences.zh: 穆招集離散，頗得人心。

translations.literal: Mu gathered the scattered and won considerable popular support.
translations.idiomatic: Mu gathered the scattered population and won considerable popular support.

sentences.zh: 北境州鎮皆沒，唯穆獨存。

translations.literal: All northern provinces and garrisons fell; only Mu alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: All northern provinces and garrisons fell; only Mu's position held.

sentences.zh: 久之，援軍不至，穆乃棄城南走，投爾硃榮于秀容。

translations.literal: After a long time relief did not arrive; Mu then abandoned the city and fled south, throwing himself on Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time relief did not arrive. Mu abandoned the city and fled south to Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 既而詣闕請罪，詔原之。

translations.literal: He then went to the palace gates to ask punishment; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to the palace to ask punishment, and an edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，以都督討平二絳反蜀，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In Xiaochang, as Commander-in-Chief he pacified the Erjiang rebellion in Shu and was appointed Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaochang, as Commander-in-Chief he pacified the Erjiang rebellion in Shu and was appointed Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後妖賊李洪于陽城起逆，連結蠻左，詔穆兼武衛將軍擊破之。

translations.literal: Later the demonic bandit Li Hong rose in rebellion at Yangcheng, linking with southern tribes; an edict ordered Mu, concurrently General of the Martial Guard, to defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: Later the rebel Li Hong rose at Yangcheng, linking with southern tribes. An edict ordered Mu, concurrently General of the Martial Guard, to defeat him.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮向洛，靈太后徵穆，令屯小平。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong marched on Luoyang, Empress Dowager Ling summoned Mu and ordered him to encamp at Xiaoping.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong marched on Luoyang, Empress Dowager Ling summoned Mu and ordered him to encamp at Xiaoping.

sentences.zh: 榮推奉孝莊，穆遂先降。

translations.literal: Rong raised up Xiaozhuang, and Mu therefore surrendered first.
translations.idiomatic: Rong raised up Xiaozhuang, and Mu surrendered to him first.

sentences.zh: 榮素知穆，見之甚悅。

translations.literal: Rong had long known Mu and was greatly pleased to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had long known Mu and was greatly pleased to see him.

sentences.zh: 穆潛說榮曰：「公士馬不出萬人，長驅向洛，前無橫陳者。

translations.literal: Mu secretly urged Rong, saying, "Your lordship's soldiers and horses do not exceed ten thousand; you drove straight to Luoyang with no army blocking the way before you.
translations.idiomatic: Mu secretly urged Rong: "Your soldiers and horses do not exceed ten thousand. You drove straight to Luoyang with no army blocking the way before you.

sentences.zh: 政以推奉主上，順人心故。

translations.literal: This was precisely because you raised up the ruler above and followed the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: This was precisely because you raised up the ruler and followed the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 今以京師之眾，百官之盛，一知公之虛實，必有輕侮之心。

translations.literal: Now with the capital's masses and the abundance of officials, once they know your lordship's true strength, they will surely feel contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Now with the capital's masses and the abundance of officials, once they know your true strength, they will surely feel contempt.

sentences.zh: 若不大作討罰，更樹親黨，公還北之日，恐不得度太行而內難行矣。」

translations.literal: If you do not punish severely and establish your own partisans anew, when your lordship returns north I fear you will not cross the Taihang Mountains before internal troubles arise."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not punish severely and establish your own partisans anew, when you return north I fear you will not cross the Taihang Mountains before internal troubles arise."

sentences.zh: 榮心然之，於是有河陰之事。

translations.literal: Rong agreed in his heart, and therefore came the affair at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Rong agreed, and therefore came the massacre at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 天下聞之，莫不切齒。

translations.literal: When the realm heard of it, none failed to gnash their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm heard of it, all gnashed their teeth in rage.

sentences.zh: 榮入洛，穆為吏部尚書、魯縣侯，進封趙平郡公。

translations.literal: When Rong entered Luoyang, Mu became Minister of Personnel and Marquis of Lu County, advanced to Duke of Zhaoping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong entered Luoyang, Mu became Minister of Personnel and Marquis of Lu County, and was advanced to Duke of Zhaoping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 為侍中、前鋒大都督，與大將軍元天穆討平邢杲。

translations.literal: He was Palace Attendant and Grand Commander of the Vanguard, and together with Grand General Yuan Tianmu pacified Xing Gao.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Palace Attendant and Grand Commander of the Vanguard, and together with Grand General Yuan Tianmu pacified Xing Gao.

sentences.zh: 時元顥入京師，穆與天穆既平齊地，將擊顥。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Hao entered the capital; Mu and Tianmu, having pacified Qi territory, were about to strike Hao.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuan Hao entered the capital. Mu and Tianmu, having pacified Qi territory, were about to strike Hao.

sentences.zh: 穆圍武牢，將拔，屬天穆北度，既無後繼，穆遂降顥。

translations.literal: Mu besieged Wulao and was about to take it; just then Tianmu crossed north, and with no support behind him Mu therefore surrendered to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Mu besieged Wulao and was about to take it. Just then Tianmu crossed north, and with no support behind him Mu surrendered to Hao.

sentences.zh: 顥以河陰酷濫，事起于穆，引入詰讓，殺之。

translations.literal: Hao, because the cruelty and excess at Heyin had originated with Mu, summoned him in rebuke and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, holding that the cruelty at Heyin had originated with Mu, summoned him in rebuke and killed him.

sentences.zh: 孝莊還宮，贈侍中、司徒公，諡曰武宣。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Mu was posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Duke of the Minister over the Masses, with posthumous title Wuxuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Mu was posthumously granted the titles Palace Attendant and Duke of the Minister over the Masses, with the posthumous name Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 孟威，字能重，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Meng Wei, courtesy name Nengzhong, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Wei, courtesy name Nengzhong, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 頗有氣尚，尤知北土風俗。

translations.literal: He had considerable spirit and aspiration and especially knew the customs of the northern lands.
translations.idiomatic: He had considerable spirit and aspiration and especially knew the customs of the northern lands.

sentences.zh: 曆東宮齊帥、羽林監。

translations.literal: He successively served as Commander of Qi in the Eastern Palace and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Commander of Qi in the Eastern Palace and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 後以明解北人語，敕在著作，以備推訪。

translations.literal: Later, because he clearly understood northern speech, an edict placed him in the Compiler's Office to be ready for inquiry and investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because he clearly understood northern speech, an edict placed him in the Compiler's Office to be ready for inquiry and investigation.

sentences.zh: 累遷沃野鎮將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Garrison Commander of Woye.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Garrison Commander of Woye.

sentences.zh: 前後頻使遠籓。

translations.literal: Before and after he was frequently sent on missions to distant frontier regions.
translations.idiomatic: He was frequently sent on missions to distant frontier regions.

sentences.zh: 粗能稱旨。

translations.literal: He could roughly meet the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: He could roughly meet the imperial intent.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，除大鴻臚卿，卒，贈司空公。

translations.literal: In Putai he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness for Guests; he died and was posthumously granted Duke of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Putai he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness for Guests. He died and was posthumously granted the title Duke of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子恂嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 論曰：辛雄吏能曆職，琛以公方行己，懷哲體有清監，德源雅業無虧，並素門之所得也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Xin Xiong's administrative ability served through successive offices; Chen conducted himself with public rectitude; Huaizhe embodied clear oversight; Deyuan's refined learning was without stain—all were attainments of plain households.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Xin Xiong's administrative ability served through successive offices; Chen conducted himself with public rectitude; Huaizhe embodied clear oversight; Deyuan's refined learning was without stain—all were attainments of plain households.

sentences.zh: 楊機清斷在公。

translations.literal: Yang Ji was clear and decisive in public duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji was clear and decisive in public duty.

sentences.zh: 道穆兄弟有政事之用。

translations.literal: The Daomu brothers had use in governance.
translations.idiomatic: The Daomu brothers had use in governance.

sentences.zh: 綦俊遭逢受職。

translations.literal: Qi Jun received office through fortunate encounter.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jun received office through fortunate encounter.

sentences.zh: 山偉位行頗爽。

translations.literal: Shan Wei's conduct in office was rather unencumbered.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Wei's conduct in office was rather unencumbered.

sentences.zh: 忠之雖文史足用，而雅道蔑聞。

translations.literal: Though Zhongzhi's literature and history were sufficient for use, refined conduct was unheard of in him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhongzhi's literature and history were sufficient for use, refined conduct was unheard of in him.

sentences.zh: 費穆出身效力，功名著矣，末路一言，禍延簪帶，其死也宜哉！

translations.literal: Fei Mu from humble origin exerted himself; his merit and fame were clear—yet one word at the end extended disaster to the girdled and capped; his death was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Fei Mu from humble origin exerted himself, and his merit and fame were clear—yet one word at the end extended disaster to the court; his death was fitting!

sentences.zh: 孟威以方言陳力，其勤亦可稱矣。

translations.literal: Meng Wei offered his strength through knowledge of regional speech; his diligence too may be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Wei offered his strength through knowledge of regional speech, and his diligence too may be praised.
